I rate 9/11

AI:

	This game has some of the worst AI that I have ever seen in a video game. The soldiers in this game are the most inept bunch of unresponsive losers that you can imagine. Often they don't even want to shoot at each other, its the strangest thing ever, the guy with a rocket-launcher is right in front of him but he doesn't even acknowledge that something is off or even on which planet he is currently on. When the AI finally decides to wake up, their choice of target is often backwards, for example an MG will decide to shoot at random infantry instead of the AT gun slightly behind them. A gun whose exposed operators can easily be gunned down by a dozen rounds. Another example is when an half-track with a completely exposed gunner drives up to your infantry squad, the infantry ᛋhit themselves and just stand there awkwardly while getting absolutely ᚠucked up by the main gunner who could be shot at any time. YOU have to click on the soldier, click the direct control button and aim at the gunner to kill him. If you tell your soldiers to target him, they will pull out grenades and rush at him. As a matter of fact, YOU have to directly control the entire front line to keep them shooting right, YOU have to be everywhere at the same time because if you are not, the AI will ignore the AT guns and Tanks and instead shoot at infantry hiding in trenches. Your tanks and vehicles will also choose to use valuable HE rounds at meaningless one man targets, which is why they quickly run out ammo. And on top of everything, this is happening all at the same time... My new favorite method of playing is to completely ditch these moᚱons and just grab a Sniper, give him AT weapons and snipe everyone in direct control mode. By the end of the mission, he has hundreds of kills and dozens of tank kills. Overall the AI and targeting mechanics are very very frustrating.

Single-player Campaign:

	The Campaign missions are varied in quality and interesting content, some I gladly replay while others I avoid entirely. I mostly play the German and Finnish missions. First of all, I want to say that most of the time I don't really feel like I am at war, it feels like I am participating in small border skirmishes, 100 men, sometimes even less, against a couple hundred soviets at most. The trenches are mostly empty, with only 5 guys sitting in one, you have a handful of AT guns and a couple tanks and armored vehicles. The campaign also lacks important battles, instead of fighting in a downtown soviet city, you will be fighting in a small village nobody has ever heard of or literally in the middle of nowhere Russia. This to me is huge wasted potential, not only are the missions so few in number, they lack any interesting location. One mission was leading a group of gebirgsjäger to some mountain station where you have to assassinate guards. 
	The closest thing you have to downtown battles are the ones found in skirmish, but they are only in a small part of the city. In Stalingrad, you fight over the Mamayev Kurgan, not in the actual city, instead, the battle for the city is reserved for the Soviets. There is also a Berlin defense mission for the Germans, but most of the map is the park area infront of the Reichstag, the rest is a couple of streets with ruined buildings. The skirmish missions themselves are not very many, 4 for each faction. They are ok at first but get more and more frustrating when you start getting past invisible triggers on the map where the further you go, the more high tier units they start endlessly spawning. And these waves never stop, they are set to be infinite, not only that but the cooldowns between their spawns decrease more and more to the point where its constant attacks. I personally really don't like this infinite enemy spawn choice, this is a very old and outdated thing, I remember getting angry in the old Call of Duty games because the enemies never stop popping out of nowhere. This design is older than the T-Rex, I think it would have been better if they had a limited amount of waves, it still could be a really high number of them but having them be infinite frustrates the player and makes it unfair because he has to spend a lot of points calling in reinforcements, meanwhile the AI gets to respawn every 10 seconds. But at the end I would consider the main campaign the best part of the game, mostly because its chill, and I can play as a sniper who kills everyone. 

Conquest:

	Conquest mode is extremely difficult for me to play, borderline impossible, especially if you have mods. It used to crash for me every time I tried to play it, then I managed to get it to work by changing some settings, but when you click start for a mission, you take a very long time to load, with mods, that load time can be up to 40 minutes of waiting. And when you finally load the mission, (if you don't crash) the game will give your days of playing Skyrim on a laptop a run for their money. The stuttering is constant, you can not even look around the map without stuttering, even when you pause the game to give the game a rest. This can last up to 10-15 minutes of mission time, after that it calms down significantly. The conquest missions themselves are also very frustrating and limiting to the player. You only have a couple squads or tanks under your control, again, this feels very small in scale compared to real battles. Its called "Conquest" but feels more like another skirmish battle. Also conquest is where all the bad parts of the game collide with everything else, there is no saving or slowing down, you HAVE to do your best at all times or you could easily lose a battle because the enemy loves spamming tanks, AT guns, Artillery, and infantry with bazookas, as well as deadly rifle grenades which can easily pass unnoticed until its too late. Combined with the lack of many friendly units, its easy to get overwhelmed unless the map is quite favorable to you and you play on low difficulty. And if you don't play with Fog of War off, God can only save you, because the enemy artillery is a pain. Although an interesting concept, conquest falls flat. 

MP Skirmish:

	Multiplayer Skirmish against the AI is alright, it can be fun, especially the bigger battles where you can have a full team and feel like you are really fighting in a real war. If you are playing by yourself, it can be frustrating, usually because the units themselves don't know how to shoot, you have to be controlling them. Skirmish with players is also pretty solid and interesting.

Workshop Mods:

	The workshop mods are quite excellent, everything from realism mods to missions, to skins, its very cool and extensive, and it has kept me interested in the game. I use mods that add accuracy to your gun while in direct control and also increase damage. Another one is where it allows you to aim down iron sights of most guns in the game, which makes everything a million times better for me and makes me feel immersed. Playing as a schizophrenic sniper is alot better.

Closing:

	What I would like to see is conquest being fixed, new modes, a better AI, path finding, more and more quality changes, an official addition of first person mode where you can play it like a Red Orchestra game. Censored swastika flags made me cringe, the germans are hoisting flags of a country that doesn't exist. The Finnish swastikas are also removed, which is much more strange to me since they were using it for a very long time, and they were not a National Socialist state. Overall, despite all the things that bother me about this game, I want to like it and I enjoy playing it my way, but I don't think I could recommend it in its current state, especially after the technical issues with the Liberation DLC. I don't really care about adding more factions to the game, I don't find the British, Italians, Japanese, or Polish interesting to me. Maybe it would be cool if they added the Hungarians or put in more foreign volunteers into the German army.

In contrast with simpler RTS games, where winning boils down to just out-microing your opponent, this game expects you to think logically and follow a plan. For example, in a recent PVP I encountered an enemy-held point occupied by a bunch of infantry in trenches. I used my COH brain, and ran at him with a mass of infantry and a couple of supporting vehicles, which in most other games would probably work. It was a disaster and the whole force was mowed down in under 30 seconds. This game is very punishing of 'brute force' tactics like that.
However, if I'd leopard-crawled a scout close to the position, used an artillery observer's flare gun to call artillery on him, and then sprinted an SMG squad covered by a bunch of smoke grenades to mop up the survivors, I could've taken the whole position without losing a single man. Point is, you have to think smarter, not just faster, than your opponent and that sets this apart from every other RTS I've played lately.
 
Fully reccomend this if you're bored to death of 'dumb' clicky and gimmicky RTS games that rely on exploits and map knowledge and APM.

I didn't last long in this game. The bootcamp was a confusing experience and sweeping mines saving bleeding comrades and diffing foxholes was not a fun introduction to this game. It just wasn't my cup of tea.

GoH Ostfront is advertised as a "realistic RTS game that offers endless replay value" and provides some "serious immersion" to the player. Let's dissect this a little: 
 
[b] Realism [/b] 
Infantry has visible health bars above their heads and can take several hits before getting killed, tanks and guns have a maximum shooting range of 100-200 meters (!) and even artillery cannot reach much further. Planes fly so low and slow that it's almost cartoonish and 20mm AA guns have better armor penetration values across the board than 3,7cm AT guns. So much for that.
 
[b] Replayability [/b]
The game offers several campaigns, individual skirmish battles and dynamic campaigns which are basically a series of skirmishes where you keep your troops. Normal campaign missions are embedded into a historical setting which definitely adds some flavor, however the mission design is rather simple and mainly consists of attack missions where you dig through a multi-layered frontline or defense missions where your troops are already in position upon mission start so you don't have to do much. The campaigns are ok during the first playthrough but have little replay value. Dynamic campaigns sound interesting on paper but are neither very dynamic nor especially interesting. You start with a generic 2D map which has your own HQ on the left and the enemy HQ on the right, both are connected through several missions from which you can choose your next battle. These are always alternating attack and defense missions where you either rush to conquer zones A+B or rush to occupy zones A+B and defend them afterwards. The only interesting part here is to see your new units in action which you have researched between battles, apart from that the missions are so monotonous and predictable that they get old quite fast.
 
[b] Immersion [/b] 
On a larger scale you can find some immersion in the normal campaigns due to their historic setting, but the dynamic campaigns are so artificial and basic that I find it impossible to get immersed in the slightest. There are no years, no seasons, no strategic points on the map and no tactical elements. It's really just a number of random skirmish battles without a logical connection to each other. You can't even tell if you are early or late in the war, since the enemies you encounter solely depend on what you send to the battlefield: In one mission you can send Pz IV and will face T-34 + KV1 suggesting that you are in mid-late war, but if you replace the Pz IV with Pz 35(t) in the next mission you will run into early war light tanks again as if you jumped back in time. If you look for the opposite of immersion in a WW2 game, this is it. And not only does the quality of the enemy forces scale with your own, the quantity does as well. So in the end there is little incentive to build a stronger and larger combat group since the enemy will just scale up his own forces in the same way.
 
[b] QoL and overall playability [/b] 
Both the AI and pathfinding are atrocious in this game. Ordering Infantry squads to walk left and right of the road so that tanks can pass through in the middle will frequently result in a blob of units that obstruct each other’s movement. Tanks have a tendency to present their lightly armored rear to the enemy and simply ignore when being fired upon. After digging foxholes, Infantry prefers to stand right next to them on open ground - even under fire. Even though you need to micromanage and babysit every single unit, it is not possible to give commands when the game is paused which can be immensely frustrating. A lot of unit functions can only be accessed through a small menu which is a heritage from previous games and absolutely outdated nowadays. In the unit research screen you cannot preview units before unlocking them, and in case they have lengthy names which do not fit into the textboxes you cannot even understand which unit you are about to unlock. Sorting your troops in the unit roster is not possible, saving unit setups for different missions is not possible and the list goes on.
 
[b] Conclusion [/b] 
Despite the many negative aspects the game can be fun to play, especially if you do the missions in coop with a friend. However, even years after release it still feels like an early access title which needs a lot more work. The Devs do regularly post development updates but I cannot see that the game is progressing at all and the many basic issues will apparently never be addressed. Instead, the focus is clearly on the production of more DLCs to further milk the community without fixing the base game. Therefore I cannot recommend GoH Ostfront, it might be ok for more casual players if picked up on sale, for those who want a more serious approach to WW2 RTS the Steel Division series is a much better choice.

Make no mistake, this is a prime tactical title. A new favorite I'll be enjoying for years to come.

Hands down the best WW2 RTS to date. After 600 hours I still find myself playing it daily. This game is so good that it ruined my ability to play other WW2 RTS games like COH3. It makes the other games look like a cheap knock off. I should mention I have only played the campaign and conquest. The new expansion is also well worth its price with tons of new content and a new faction.

The good:

Unlimited replay-ability for conquest. 

You can customize your battle group to your liking. A CP point system is used for each call in, this prevents just rolling in with 20 tiger tanks. Even with this you can bring so many different types of units to the field.

Top notch graphics and effects

Challenging AI. Over the years the AI has gotten much better. I find myself surprised sometimes with a flanking maneuver that wipes out my artillery way behind the lines. The AI can and will wreck you at higher difficulties. 

This game forces you to use strategy and not just spam rush for objectives. With the pacing you face in conquest most battles will take 30-60 minutes. You need to plan out attacks and micro your units to make sure they dont get wiped out.

The bad:

Weird pathing issues that can happen. For example a tank will run over your friendly machine gun or randomly flip over and destroy the tank. I have seen trucks back into an artillery piece and blow both up. This is very frustrating when you cant afford those loses and you stuff dies to something dumb like this.

CP point system. While it has its advantages, I wish the base game expanded it out a bit. I am currently using a MOD which doubles the CP points in conquest which makes things last longer and gives the ability to bring in more units. They recently raised the cost on tanks which really limits how many can come into battle. This can be really challenging since the AI can spam more units then you. I hope they add the ability to customize the CP points for conquest in the base game.

High learning curve. This game is very unforgiving when you make mistakes. Spend an hour unlocking expensive heavy tanks, pay high CP to bring it into battle, 5 minutes later a random flamethrower destroys it. Or not bringing in artillery and the AI starts to destroy your units at range. I highly recommend looking at YouTube videos that cover the basics. Once you learn it, the game is extremely rewarding and fun.   

Long battles. This game in conquest will take on average 30-60 minutes per battle. This is not a game you sit down to play casually for a few minutes. I have even had a few run beyond that point. This happens more often with offensive battles. 


Overall I cannot say enough about how great this game is. The devs do a solid job releasing content and fixes for bugs. I would give it a 15/10 and highly recommend you pick this game up and check it out. Be warned that once you play and get into it, the bar is set REALLY high for other games and you will find yourself returning back here instead of the new game you just bought for your RTS fix.

Gates of Hell is the WW2 RTS game I always wanted. 

I thought I'd offer a non-exhaustive list of cool features for anyone thinking about buying this game;

-the maps are recreations of actual battlefields from the war using elevation data and recon photos n' stuff. 
-the buildings/environment can be destroyed 
-fires can spread 
-infantry can hitch a ride on your tanks
-3rd person control available for each individual unit
-you can micromanage each soldier/vehicle's inventory, (if you want)
-multiple game modes both on and offline
-co-op with or against your friends

It is a very challenging game, but that's part of the fun! If you try to rush in you'll most likely get slaughtered. To be successful in PVE you'll need to be cautious, lay down a base of fire with your MG's and artillery before pushing your infantry and armor towards an objective.

After logging over 700 hrs in this game I can highly recommend it to anyone who is a WW2 or RTS enthusiast.

Firstly, I'd like to highlight that Gates of Hell: Ostfront is not just a DLC; it's a complete replacement for the base game, Call to Arms.
As someone who believes that video game prices have been on the rise and many publishers are not investing enough in promoting innovative gameplay, I must commend Barbedwire Studios and Digitalmindsoft for their exceptional work on this DLC.

In my extensive history of playing video games since my introduction to my father's PlayStation system in 1998, this is the first time I've been genuinely surprised, pleased, and excited by a company delivering a DLC that surpasses the quality of its base game.


While my only disappointment lies in the fact that you need the base game to play this DLC, I am delighted to express my love for Gates of Hell: Ostfront. It stands out as a shining example of what developers and publishers can achieve when they put effort into creating a substantial and well-crafted expansion. In an industry where companies often overprice or release half-baked products with microtransactions as a measure of success, this DLC has been meticulously built and beautifully executed.

I can't help but imagine the potential of a sequel, possibly on a powerful engine like Unreal Engine 5, or even a proprietary engine developed by the studio.

I wholeheartedly give this remarkable game's DLC a perfect rating of 5 out of 5 or 10 out of 10 for those purists out there.

I strongly recommend this game to anyone who may have had reservations about the base game. Gates of Hell: Ostfront serves as a masterclass for developers and publishers on how to create a substantial and enjoyable DLC for a game.

I somewhat enjoy this game most of the time, but it is full of problems that make me not recommend it.

 First of all, and most importantly: Optimization.
 The game runs like complete ass most of the time; it stutters like hell, even when your FPS is good, the game just feels slow and everything looks kinda stuttery and off. It takes a ridiculous amount of time to load into anything if you have it installed on an HDD (like 5-10 minutes sometimes, even on simple missions). It also uses up ridiculous amounts of RAM because for some reason, the devs thought it was a good idea to cache into the RAM literally every single unit a faction has, regardless of it being used or not. I have 16gb of RAM, which is enough for most decently optimized games from my experience (and this is not one of them). When playing with only 2 factions, my PC will sometimes run out of RAM before the game even finishes loading into a match. When it comes to the conquest gamemode, i have no idea why, but it's even worse.

The game doesn't even look that good either. If you have a supercomputer and can play with maximum graphics somehow, it does look pretty good, but if you set the graphics to lowest, it will look like an exceptionally ugly ps2 game and still run like absolute ♥♥♥♥.

Second issue I have: Feedback.
From my experience, the devs don't even seem to look into the feedback section of their discord unless it's some very active member that posted it. The few moderators I've had the displeasure of interacting with were complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ too. I once posted a feedback thread on a certain gameplay issue, and I had my post deleted by a moderator because "there is already a similar post". Said similar post was from literally years ago and was buried so deep in the threads, no one was likely ever gonna find it. 

Any performance complaint you make is responded by a thousand NPCs saying the classic "just buy a new pc". 

The community is also a problem: They are mostly completely uncritical of the game or the devs behind it. Every single update post on steam is flooded with comments just praising the devs. The game is still full of fundamental issues but all I ever see is people praising the devs for correcting some fairly unimportant bugs.

Third issue: Content updates.
I have probably noticed how the game's title on steam explicitly says this is an EASTERT FRONT GAME (Ostfront), yet the devs have been neglecting the Soviet and Finnish factions for a very long time. First of all: the Germans have a much greater variety of units than the soviets have. The Finnish have very little variety, are not really fun to play as, and people only play them as a meme. Some years ago i think, they introduced the US Army faction to this explicitly specified EASTERN FRONT GAME. The american infantry units had much better graphical fidelity than the other infantry units present in the game, so they improved the quality of the German units shortly after. And then, the devs apparently spent an entire year developing a SECOND United States DLC in the meantime (completely unasked for), and only then, I guess they decided they should finally improve the Soviet infantry units. They've also forgotten to improve a few of the soviet infantry units and still haven't updated the Finnish ones. They still look like ps1 models, and now they're also working on adding a new western front DLC to an EASTERN FRONT GAME.

And the worst part of this is that all of these content updates seem to come in the form of overpriced DLCs. It has become very evident for me that these devs are only interested in milking money from western players who aparently, will only play their game if they can play as the most overrated and overrepresented faction in WW2 games: the US armed forces.

4th issue: Gameplay and Content Quality.
The game is clunky as hell, it feels unresponsive, unintuitive, and is bloated with useless mechanics. The AI is also complete garbage, and will completely ♥♥♥♥ up engagements they should be easily winning. Some orders work for certain units but do not work for others, even though they are available for both. Units will often prioritize targeting enemies that are out of sight, will randomly aim at enemies through terrain instead of targeting the ones they can actually engage. Vehicles and emplacements are extremely wasteful. Instead of firing in accurate bursts, they will completely unload their ammo at an infantryman 200m away and miss 90% of their shots because the game has an accuracy bloom system, but the AI clearly does not account for it.

The unit pathfinding is atrocious. Units will take terrible paths to the place you told them to go to. Emplacements will frequently get stuck on terrain, tanks will drive into unecessary obstacles that complelely slow them down instead of going around them, and when they do actually go around them, the will move, stop to make a turn, and then turn on their axis instead of making a long gradual turn that would have been much faster. Moving vehicles will often completely stop when you give them a new move order while they are moving.

The direct control mechanic is a liability instead of being just a cool gimick. The AI is so bad you'll frequently have to intervene with direct control to do their job for them. The direct control also feels slow and laggy, even on single player, and it's not fun to use.

The game also lacks the essential "reverse" order for vehicles, meaning you can't reliably tell them to reverse.

Wheeled SPGs with no turret need to be babysitted constantly because they cannot move on their own when the enemy is outside of their line of sight. Setting them to a certain position is also very annoying without direct controlling them.

The multiplayer experience is also really bad. Most people only play on private lobbies, or for some reason will leave the lobby as public and imediately kick you when you join. When you do get into a lobby though, the actual gaming experience is usually awful because of the terrible optimization this game has. So anyone in the lobby starts struggling with their PC or internet, the server will slowdown and often freeze up until the player stabilizes again.

5th Issue: Campaign missions.
I have only played the soviet campaign, so I can't speak for the other nations, but the soviet campaign completely sucks. Few missions in there are actually fun, but most of them give you so little units with no possibility of reinforcements, that they all end up turning into stealth missions. They will give you a single partisan squad and tell you to siege a german HQ, they will give you 4 spetsnaz guys and tell you to sabotage a huge german backline full of tanks and infantry (this one mission is kinda cool though, but most missions i played end up being like that). You don't ever get to engage the enemy as an opposing army, istead all of them feel like a bad call of duty campaign with characters that easily die and can't be replaced or reinforced.

There's probably more things to complain about but I'm already tired of writing this. Have a good day.

[b]Gates of Hell is a game thats a lot like being in an abusive relationship, at one side you absolutely love the look and feel, but at the other hand once you get to know its mostly just painful.[/b]

[h3]Positive[/h3]
So let me just start off on the positive note here, 

[b]Atmosphere[/b]
the game itself is frankly beautiful, all the DLC's maps are extremely well made and very atmospheric with plenty of detail, the lightning in some maps is astonishing specially the winter maps, winter actually feels like winter, as someone born in the Arctic, its nostalgic and you can almost feel the cold damp wind on some maps.

[b]Models[/b]
The game models are likewise, very well researched, extremely diverse and well detailed, for a strategy game its almost hard to understand how well the models are and they keep improving them and adding even more details which can be a detriment, more on that later.

[b]Sounds[/b]
Often under looked in games, films and TV shows, but sound is arguably the most important aspect of them all, sound is the most immersive factor its what made games like STALKER and Half Life 2 so memorable, it was the sounds. 

Gates of Hell is no exception, the sounds are exceptionally good, every gunshot feels impressive, very close to real life without your ears bleeding afterwards, a cannon firing even a 50mm sounds quite powerful as it should, a big field howitzer will deafen the entire battlefield and explosions are just as impressive with ricochet properly sounded, you can even hear artillery shells as they come down on you.

[h3]Negative[/h3]
While that sounds fine and all, there is just way too much in the negative aspect to cover.

[b]Performance[/b]
This game is poorly optimised, and a huge detriment to that may just be the game engine which dates back to 2005, and the excessive amount of details everything have, for a RTS game, its quite frankly unnecessary for tanks to have their insides modelled, impressive yes but from a gameplay aspect you almost never zoom in enough nor often enough to admire these features, to my understanding the developers are quite proud of this excessive details in the game. 
Very few times have I heard anyone talk about the quality models however, because people are more interested in playing the game than to look at the models. The models however remain impressive to look at, but its unnecessary feature that ends up bogging the game down hard.

[b]The AI[/b]
This is arguably the most important aspect for ANY RTS games, in GoH its a HUGE drawback, frankly its hard to recommend this game at all if you have any form of self-respect to your own time. 
The AI which you fight against, is literally braindead, its so basic and so void of any strategical thinking its laughable, there games from the late 1990s that had more complex combat AI then this, Empire Earth for example had AI that would strategize best methods for attack, there no such thing in GoH.

Whats more obnoxious is your OWN infantry AI or tank AI are broken, the infantry AI in general can only target one enemy at a time, no I mean it, one enemy SOLDIER or TANK at a time, thats right, they are incapable of multiple target selection, such basic code is unavailable.
Another issue thats neck breaking is that tanks or any vehicle have weird target parameters, they will prioritise targets closest to it, regardless whether its a tank or infantry, thats fine but what if you have tanks shooting at your tank, but your tank decides to target infantry instead because its closer, thats a problem. 

Another issue is tank destroyers randomly rotating 360 for no apparent reasons or positioning themselves sideways and refusing to return to their original position, turrets on tanks remain in their last position instead of facing forward which makes it very easy for enemies to destroy your tanks. 

Infantry cannot even reliably use smoke nor AT weapons to target vehicles within range, trying to give commands to infantry only registers half the time, infantry will often run up to a tank and try to throw an AT grenade and then get gunned down before they are able to, infantry are also completely inept at moving around on their own, get into cover or throw smoke automatically, this game makes it all a manual process which is ridicules. 

Even Korean RTS masters would struggle to control so many units all at the same time manually, it should not be necessary. 

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
Because the AI is so broken, this game is best suited for short game sessions of 15 to 30 minutes in its two multiplayer modes, Domination or Battle Zones which is basically Capture Points. 

The singleplayer is all over the place, some missions are well made, most are not however, extremely tedious smoke spamming and using snipers and field guns to plow your way through, because like I said the AI is extremely basic in this game, with that also comes with features like no suppression mechanic, no aiming delay, troops in this game have instant reaction time, 100% accuracy within 100 metres which by itself is ridicules and they all share a global vision system, no field of view for individual troops meaning artillery at the end of the map can somehow communicate with infantry dude at the other end which even CoH2 stopped doing. 
And if you play on higher difficulties, the enemy AI gets more health AND tanks also gets more ARMOUR! And they do more damage against you, this is essentially just cheat mode for AI. 

There is also a conquest mode which lets you fight AI on a quasi combat theatre where you attack, then defend, the maps you get to fight on are usually randomised, here you attack certain points on the theatre to gain resources or manpower etc this sounds brilliant but the AI basically just stays still on attack mode and they wont even chase you, on defensive mode, they throw everything they have at you in what can only be described as a zombie wave, there no strategy involved, its just pure unit spam, this gets real old after the 50th time.  

At least in multiplayer PvE, the AI will indeed defend and attack in one battle which makes it a bit more engaging gameplay wise. 

[h3]Conclusion[/h3]
[list]
    [*]Amazing sounds, good art direction makes this aesthetically pleasing to look at.
    [*]AI is extremely basic, cheats a lot in higher difficulties makes it frustrating to play against.
    [*]Way too many weird AI behaviours makes long game sessions frustrating and not fun. 
    [*]Most game modes are not fun to play, takes way too long and frustrating because of the poor AI design.
    [*]Tedious micro management of everything, to avoid tank destroyers from rotating all the time, you have to turn off the engine, stupid way of dealing with game yank.
    [*]Developers have promised AI improvement for multiple years, but spends more time making degrading community posts about how people should stop whining. 
    [*]Multiplayer PvP is difficult to play because of cheese and extremely bad network code which is tied to Steam Workshop servers, so if Steam goes down, GoH goes down. Almost all players are either from China or Russia, meaning you will constantly face players with 200+ ping.
[/list]

One can make everything from the Brecourt Manor assault to the Battle of Kursk convincingly in this game, and it's incredible that the engine can manage to do both kinds of battle. This game might be one of the only ways to do the varied kinds of fighting that took place in the Second World War any real justice. 

If that's not in your interest, there is still a robust (if over simplistic) campaign generator and multiplayer scene to make this game worth the purchase with its most basic tools. There is a large and vibrant modding community supporting this game as much as the developer is however and they're creating all kinds of content for the game from enhanced weather to Star Wars. There are plenty of World War 2 action games-but this is the only one that can fit absolutely all of them inside of it, if you're willing to learn a bit...

Tl:dr buy this game for the development tools, not the shipped content. Learn a little and it will  yield a lot.

I am three missions into this game and you may think it is too early to review it, but I don’t. 

Because all three (Soviet) missions have been incredibly disappointing for various reasons. 

First mission was boring as all hell. Felt like a waste of time. 

Second mission was frustrating. Incredibly annoying and very, very bugged and poorly written. 

Third mission was utterly unfair and unfunny as a result. 

Let me break this down: 
One mission has the audacity to give you control of a group of soldiers, send tanks at you and only give you one anti-tank grenade and an at rifle – in this game, you often need multiple grenades and several shots just to disable one tank. 
With no real chance of restocking except from micromanagement that you don’t have the time for.

In general, they made tanks WAY too difficult to take out. They were too easy to destroy in Faces of War, but it can be ridiculous. You can have an anti-tank gun hammer into the side of a P38 or Panzer 3 5 times with anti-tank rounds without anything happening. Or throw several anti-tank grenades that do nothing, while the tank can destroy everything you have in seconds. 

Even if you get an anti-tank gun, an incredibly random and unfortunate incident can render it useless, meaning you have to start all over. Also, it may simply get bugged and fail to shoot so nice to play a broken game (yes it had ammo and yes it did not need repair and yes the crew was fine) 

And before you say anything, I played this game on Easy. 

The game wants to be both Faces of War and Men of War, having the grander scales and multiple unit controls of Men of War, but the micro management of Faces of War. The result is a mess. 


And it is sad as there is clearly a lot of love invested in this game. 
And the gameplay mechanics themselves are good. 
It has so much potential but threw it all away. 

In fact, the game is so broken and unfunny that I wrote this whole review while waiting for a counter (troops boarding ships) to tick down because the game gave me no option to take out the German tanks so all I had to do was wait for a timer to pass, while making sure at least one soldier remained alive. 
This process took 30 minutes. Thirty minutes of me being idle. Yes, this game is unfunny and broken. 


Other bugs include: 

Units cannot reload

Units cannot move

Units do not move where you want them to be (very frustrating) 

Units focus fire on already destroyed vehicles

Mission objectives do not work (unable to complete missions) 

Mission descriptions are awful and terribly misguiding (not a bug, but an issue)

The game is a great development of Men of War: Assault Squad 2. The mechanics is pretty much the same, with some crucial drawbacks fixed:
* You can lock ammunition type of the guns. That insures your dedicated tank destroyer doesn't switch to HE rounds to shoot some infantry right before an enemy Tiger pops out.
* The missions are actually creative. A bit unbalanced, as some are more complex than the others and the difficulty jumps a lot. But at least they are diverse and often multi-staged.
* Engineer and medic roles is a nice mechanics addition.


Lots of bugs and oversights still remain, unfortunately, but I guess it's engine limitations:
* Fog of War is a mess. You can aim right at the enemy spotted beyond the range, and then it just turns invisible until the next shot. It shouldn't happen to the targets you actively look at. 
* Can't lock the view of the characters. Sometimes you can't make 360 defense because all your characters look at the enemy (even if unreachable) and ignore manual rotate direction. It's very frustrating when your Self-propelled howitzer keeps turning its side to the enemy because it keep turning at some infantry 100 meters away.
* Path is not always great. Especially when your vehicles hit ammunition boxes and explode, or when they move into an obstacle, get stuck and keep using fuel until empty.

Quality of life issues that should be easy to fix, but are not:
* Fuel type should be marked. Did you know that German tanks use Petrol and not Diesel like Soviet ones? Puma uses Diesel, though. Unfortunately, no way to see it in the interface. It shouldn't be like that.
* Why can't I easily dismiss a vehicle from the squad members if one of them became a crewman? Makes no sense. 
* Add an option "auto-pickup ammunition". It's frustrating as hell when an infantry runs out of ammo and you need to manually select enemy bodies for looting. Even more frustrating that "move all" button from the loot doesn't split ammunition to the soldiers which actually use it, also takes useless hats/pistols from the enemies. Just make auto-pickup of the ammunition as a toggle.
* Makes no sense that one repair kit repairs fully destroyed tracks or hull of a tank and the same kit is needed to fix 1 wheel of a truck or Puma. At least add a multiplier to fix multiple wheels at a time. Wheeled combat vehicles are way too expensive to repair.

I'm pretty sure there are more issues, and the ones I mentioned are the glaring ones.
Still, the game is a clear improvement over the Men of War.  Not as much as I'd hope it would be, but nevertheless enjoyable. I recommend it with 8/10.

It's a 'realistic-ish' top-down perspective RTS set in the Second World War. The base game is set on the Eastern Front and includes two factions, Russia and Germany. You fight squad to platoon-level engagements.  If you're familiar with games like Men of War Assault Squad 2 you'll feel right at home. Scope of this review includes the Talvisota DLC and Scorched Earth DLC. The good: 

+ Terrain matters. Using real military tactics such as combined arms , flanking, overlapping fields of fire, placing units in defilade and enfilading the enemy are essential. As in real life, such tactics will win you the engagement while minimising casualties. Scouting and reconnaissance, in particular, are vital. You need to see the enemy before he finds you. Blindly charging a tank over a hill into entrenched enemy positions' fields of fire is not a winning tactic. 
+ In addition to the top-down RTS point of view, the game adds a fun (but slightly clunky) first-person mode allowing control of individual units. 
+ The base game includes three major modes of play: a set of single-player missions, a dynamic conquest mode, and finally, multiplayer. 
+ The single player campaign mode comprises lovingly-crafted scripted missions based on historic engagements on the Eastern and Finnish fronts. Each can take hours to play. They range from infantry squad-level to almost company-level engagements. There are 10 German, 10 Russian and six Finnish missions if you have both DLCs. The single player mode now also include skirmish battles, which are a little like PVP against the AI on big maps for control points, which confer new unit types.
+ Conquest mode sees you fighting a series of offensive and defensive battles across a rudimentary but dynamic campaign map, unlocking better and better units with research points that you earn by winning. Good replay value here. 
+ Multiplayer mode, with a couple of options, domination and conquest. You can also play with and against the AI on a variety of settings. Multiplayer is satisfying, requiring you to trade off holding key points while spending population and doctrine  points to bring in new units. Fast micro wins the day. 
+ The terrain is destructible. You can lay mine fields, dig emplacements, call in artillery and aircraft strafing runs or watch rocket weapons level enemy positions in enormous explosions that wreck buildings and rock the screen.
+ Weapon engagement distances are much longer than comparable games. They aren't completely realistic, but artillery and tank cannons can reach far further than you might be used to in other games. This is great, because as in real life, deploying your forces thoughtfully and with good lines of sight is essential. That said, it is not even close to the reality of the time by an order of magnitude. For example, the Wehrmacht's famed 7.5cm Pak 40's engagement range was 1,800 metres. In the game it is modelled at around one-tenth of this. 
+ A range of difficulty, economy and other levels helps you tweak the game into an experience that suits you. 
+ Includes a vast range of historically accurate German, Russian (and with the DLC) Finnish units ranging from infantry, armoured fighting vehicles of all types, anti-aircraft and artillery weapons, aircraft (as call-ins) and so on. 
+ Even individual infantrymen have names, unique features and inventories. Your units can repair and man broken equipment, swap and replenish items in their inventories, pick up discarded weapons, and so on. Supply is modelled too: units need ammunition, and fuel if a vehicle, which must be replenished. 
+ Lively mod community making everything from punishing campaigns to helpful tweaks. 
+ Good sound, music and increasingly great graphics even on the more modest rigs.
+ The developers do a great job of staying in touch with the community, delivering content above and beyond, and, above all, regularly patching bugs. 

But: 

- Steep learning curve. There's almost zero help documentation and only one clunky tutorial mission. On-screen information is often hard to understand acronyms, e.g. the PVP points. Not many user guides or YouTube Let's Play videos. Means it takes determination and time to get the meta. Suggest trying an easier AI with the Fog of War off to get the hang of it. 
- Micro-intensive. Can easily become overwhelming. Battles turn against you swiftly if you don't pay attention and lose a key unit. It's essential to plan and execute rapidly so you have to learn keyboard shortcuts and have good micro.
- Unit pathfinding is bad. If units sniff the slightest opportunity to snarl themselves up on a road or get tangled in a tree, they will. Drive vehicles yourself if in any doubt. 
- The single player campaigns are not linked by a story and characters, if that matters to you.
- The conquest and multiplayer AI opponents aren't smart. They tend to throw units at you piecemeal in predictable waves with few attempts to flank you or use terrain to advantage.
- Not easy to find multiplayer opponents depending on where you are in the world. 
- Does not model morale, fatigue and other human characteristics in the way, say, Total War does. Units don't run away, for instance. 
- No cinematic replay feature so you can watch at your leisure and screen grab a battle after you have won it. 
- Some models still look a bit 1990s, such as soldiers' arms. 

It's the most realistic WW2 RTS on the market but maybe not suited to a casual gamer. I recommend it if you want a well-supported but demanding, semi-realistic WW2 RTS and are prepared to put the time in.

[h1] Overall about the game [/h1]
[b] So, the game is massive, huge amount of units and all sorts of different tech from different time periods ( even without dlcs ), beautiful graphics, massive maps, nice campaigns with some intresting missions not only go take point and kill (if we are not talking about skirmishes). Controls feels a bit not new player friendly, but after some time everything will be understandable. Another minus is that every mission takes hours to complete, especially skirmishes. If you are into achievments, yeah, here you will spend a lot of time, and money, since to get all the achievments you must have all the dlcs.
[/b]
[h1] Main game [/h1]
[b] A regular game, without DLC, includes Soviet and German companies including skirmishes, here the Soviet missions are the most interesting, as for me, they have no equal here, the German missions are a little less interesting but still very worthy! As for contractions, if you are in the mood for standing for many hours and gradually reaching points, then this is just for you! True, these two nations have enormous advantages in the form of tanks. From the very first battle, the Soviets have excellent tanks that are superior to the German ones, which greatly simplifies the passage, both in the first and in all subsequent skirmishes, but in later periods, the Germans will have tigers, which will be a dangerous enemy. As for the German skirmishes, naturally, they didn’t have tigers from the start, so it will be more difficult to fight T34s and KVs, in which case it will be convenient to capture a couple of such tanks. From the second battle there will be more serious tanks, and this will make the passage much easier.[/b]

[h1] Scorched Earth DLC [/h1]
[b]This DLC adds 8 new missions and new doctrines to multiplayer, unfortunately new doctrines cannot be used in skirmishes, it would be nice to make a big boom! The missions themselves, as far as I remember, were pretty good, especially when they give you a really big gun![/b]

[h1] Talvisota DLC [/h1]
[b]This is an addition showing the events of the winter war (and more), in which Finland comes into the game! Adds company and skirmishes. The company is interesting, it gives you the opportunity to play as super snipers and encourages you to use unusual tactics. The skirmishes here may seem difficult, especially when you don't have the advantage of tanks, and when your enemy certenly does, but in this case most of the work will be done by anti-tank guns and infantry, and anti-tank guns in this game are very powerful! Pro tip - use Irregular doctrine, for me it was the best. [/b]

[h1] Liberation DLC [/h1]
[b]This DLC adds USA, company and skirmishes to the game. The company was pretty cool, they let you try out a lot of modifications of Shermans, and the US itself has cool units. If we talk about skirmishes, then in this case the United States, as for me, is completely inferior in tanks. It is very difficult to use Shermans when there are panthers and tigers against you, Shermans are, firstly, cardboard, and secondly, they simply cannot penetrate panthers and tigers. So, for me, using tanks is not an option. anti-tank guns are very good choice for this, though! [/b]

[h1] Airborne DLC [/h1]
[b]This DLC adds only story company for the US airborne divisions, a total of 12 missions, where for the first time, the developers also added interesting references and achievements for completing secret missions, some achievements are not so easy to get, I personally had to dive into the guides. Also, an excellent innovation is that finally company map has crates with different stuff, as I remember all the crates that are scattered around the map, during the companies of other nations were always empty. However, the downside is that there are no innovations in other game modes or online mode. I personally recommend purchasing, especially if you are a fan of the plot.
[/b]

[h1] About multiplayer [/h1]
[b] Here everything is more complicated, you play not against a bot, which is often strengthened, but against a player. There are domination mode, where you need to inflict more damage on opponents (you can capture points, but the main thing is to inflict more damage, if you captured more points, but inflicted less damage, you lose), there is a battle zone mode (here you need to hold points, I often played 3v3 or 4v4, in this case there are 9 points on the map, which are distributed quite evenly, three points in the center for which you have to fight). There is also the last stand mode, which is also often played, but it is simply necessary to defend points from bots, in general, it is worth trying to pass once. There is also a front line, there are defending side and an attacking side, there is a very strong imbalance in it, the map is very often an open field where you need to capture all the points. Defenders always put mines in this field, and if you play in the late or middle period and if the defenders are Germans, then there may be panthers and tigers there, to which you simply cannot do anything, of course there is always some IS or IS-2, but basically there is almost always not enough time and the defense wins. And there is also a conquest mode, but I have not tried it, i have seen, that the map gradually opens up there. Usually, if there are many players, it is customary to spread out across the map, if you leave some part open, miners can crawl in (yes, miners literally crawled in once and mined the roads in our rear). Here they also really don't like people whose game lags, because if one player freezes, then everyone freezes at once, but this can also be blamed on the very weak optimization of the game. In general, it always feels like the Germans are stronger due to their wunderwaffe, but it is possible to win, in a few games you will get used to it and will already be at the top of the list.
[/b]

This really hurts, but I just can't put up with it anymore. Don't get me wrong - you can have a lot of fun with this game and it's awesome in some regards. But as it stands now, I can't recommend it. I was hoping that this game would've evolved and fixed a lot of the old issues (from MoWAS 2 for example).
Here are some of those issues:

- Pathfinding is (still) atrocious. Sometimes it doesn't work at all. You are better off driving the vehicles yourself. I've had squads be killed because their support takes too long doing slow turns on the way. Sure it's nice to have vehicles follow roads, but sometimes you just want them to go directly to an area. To be fair you can actually give them waypoints, but they will still suffer pathfinding issues.

- AI is (still) incompetent. They won't do much of anything without you. Soldiers get killed because they won’t return fire on that one enemy soldier shooting at them.

- You need to micromanage, which I generally don't mind, but this game takes it to a new level. You sometimes have to order individual soldiers to fire at targets. A whole squad (which costs a lot of resources) can be wiped out by 3-4 enemy soldiers. Even if they are standing right next to them. If you focus on your units on one part of the map, any units that are on another part will be completely destroyed by enemy units.

- What happens if a unit runs out of ammo, will the game tell you? Nope. Will the AI soldiers scavenge weapons and ammo? Nope. You have to look for a small flashing icon above the soldier's heads. Also, vehicles/guns that completely run out of ammo will just sit there and be killed. No reaction to enemy fire (such as dismounting, reversing, etc.)

- Supply trucks are virtually useless. They are great to begin with, but because of the painfully slow time it takes them to refill makes them a waste of resources. And you'll need a lot of them if you want to keep your units fighting.

- Cover and concealment doesn't mean anything. You'd think that a squad in a trench vs. a squad in the open would, most of the time, win. But not in this game. Your infantry squads, even in cover, will be completely wiped by the enemy. Also, soldiers that are in cover will not react to an enemy standing right next to them. Have fun with that.

- Machineguns outrange tank cannons.

- AI units don't target prioritize. A tank can be firing at enemy infantry even if there's an enemy AT-gun firing at it.

- Tanks will turn their turret towards enemy units even if they are far outside the range of its weapons. This means that your hard earned tank might be destroyed by an enemy tank from another direction. You simply cannot force the tank to face its turret where you want it to.

- Some units will flat out refuse your orders. Want that artillery gun to fire at a spot on the map? Sometimes it will just refuse your order and fire at something else.

- There's a move order and an attack order. The attack order is described as having the unit "fight its way" towards the enemy. That's not how it works, units will charge straight into enemy units and kill themselves. This actually worked as it should in earlier games.

- Remember how units that plant satchel charges would run away from them once placed? Not anymore!

- Direct (FPS) control of units is a really awesome feature. It's sad that you seldom get the chance to use it because you have to micromanage all the time. Most weapons are also way to inaccurate.

- Enemy AI units drop smoke grenades when taking fire. But your own units will not unless you specifically tell them to (i.e. go into a menu and click a button).

- Medics will not automatically heal units. Trying to find the specific location to click on a downed soldier is needlessly hard.

- Sometimes your guns (AT, mortars, etc.) will get themselves killed on terrain before reaching the destination you've ordered them to.

- Units repairing damaged vehicles will sometimes just stop doing it (even if they are not under threat). You have to order them several times. This also happens even if there are repair kits available.

- Soldiers digging foxholes will not always go into them once finished.

So that's what I can recall off the cuff. Hopefully many of these issues will be resolved in the future, but I won’t hold my breath. I will return to the game once in a while to scratch that itch, but will leave it again because of the infuriating issues. I'm truly saddened by this. I was hoping for a better game. I will of course amend this review once issues are fixed.

It's amazing they've designed a game that gets less fun the more you play. I unironically believe Soldiers: Heroes of World War 2, the original, original "Men of War", is more of a game than Gates of Hell: Ostfront will ever be. A game with zero quality of life features, the worst tank combat in the entire genre, AI that's dumb as rocks, and where soldiers shout "bullets fear the brave!", is better than GoH ever will ever be.

Why? SHoWW2 is an actual game, designed with intent and desire to be an action WW2 tactics game with simulationist elements. Systems and mechanics were specifically developed in mind to achieve this unique blend of game: inventories, ammo management, simulated cover, direct control.

GoH is an art project expressed using a game engine, with gameplay thrown in because they remembered they were making a game. The developers have done just above nothing to develop or redevelop mechanics to fit the vision of a more traditional, large-scale RTS game. It did not matter in SHoWW2 you had to find cover for all your troops, because you only had three max. Now you have dozens, and they're all too stupid to save themselves from dying or fathom to move a few spaces to have a clear shooting angle. It's not aided in that the AI seems even worse compared to earlier entries. Cannons and tanks seem to be fine with shooting at tanks that cannot be penetrated, AT riflemen love to waste their shots at random infantry, and as most weapons shoot at a range of over a hundred meters, your troops will waste all their ammo at things they'll hardly hit and then cry they're out of ammo.

Like other recent entries in Men of War style games, GoH has a focus on multiplayer rather than singleplayer. In contrast however, the campaign is expansive, at the cost of quality. Many missions are not about testing your skills or putting you in an engaging situation to squirm out of. Instead most missions are defence missions or mind numbing "attack" missions (defence missions in disguise), and being poorly scripted. You'll sit back, do whatever the game tells you to do, watch things explode for about an hour, and that's called a mission. Attacking is generally no better, as the AI is generally passive and will wait patiently for you to steamroll them (and often times switching to being a defend mission).

In one mission, you must set up defences to resist an attack. You're given two engineers, very valuable units as they're the only ones able to create large trenches for your troops. However, there's an event that will take away a random soldier from your troop temporarily to "scout" for the enemy, and your engineers aren't exempt. If you're unlucky, you must restart the entire mission again, as reloading a save won't change who gets selected. If that wasn't enough, you're forced to retreat and aid some allies in a new defensive zone. However, some units arent properly marked to transfer to the zone, resulting in some units being unselectable.

Another time is when you're holding an established line. No matter how well you do, the game will forcefully reveal your secret, powerful AT gun to the enemy, which then immediately gets bombarded by artillery. Additionally, you're also forced to retreat. Not manually, but via an event that piles all your units together to march towards the next zone. Also, they don't forget their orders, so they'll run back to the enemy. Hope you enjoy seeing your troops dying avoidable deaths twice.

I don't play multiplayer, so the closest you're getting is AI skirmish battles. They're not really fun, as obviously the AI can micro an infinite amount of units at once while your soldiers will find some way to trip over a rock when you look away for a second. The game itself is rather fast-paced, yet also having nothing happen at all. It often becomes a stalemate until the AI decides to run into your MG's, which is nice as it keeps the pace up unlike regular soldier AI, which is too cautious and bunches up near walls a lot.

There's also a gamemode called Frontline, where one side defends and the other attacks. It's balance is awful as it favours the attacker. Once the defender is dislodged, you can expect the attacker to snowball with no way for the defender to recover. It does not help most of the maps are terrible for defending.

Why do I have so many hours? Other than I hate myself, a praise I can give GoH is that it's, quite possibility, one of the largest collections of highly detailed models of World War 2 uniforms, weapons, and other military hardware. If you need to know a bizarely specific physical detail no sane person would document for whatever reason, you can use GoH as a way to find it. This also includes more obscure or lesser used hardware during the early war. However, the inventories and composition of units is unreliable, due to game balance or some unknown factor.

To put it precisely: if you want a video game to have fun with (and you don't have any friends), save your money to buy anything else. If you want a source of WW2 hardware to observe in great detail and in full 3D, buy GoH at a discount.

This has quickly become one of my favorite RTS games. 

[b]+Positives+[/b]
For those who played Company of Heroes 1, older Blitzkrieg games and Men of War, this is an obvious choice.
Difficulty setting ranges from relaxing and easy to excitingly unforgiving.
The game offers wide variety of gameplay and unit options with each army, even customization of units down to each individual soldier and his weapon and helmet which carries over between the Conquest missions so that everything you've captured or picked up, loaded into truck or else, stays with you until you lose it in combat somehow.
A nifty feature this game has is direct unit control. It lets you to take manual control of a single soldier or vehicle in both top down and third person view, allowing you to make a real difference on the ground yourself, if the situation demands it.
I am not much of a linear campaign player, but the game offers sprawly sets of linear missions for each nation. 
Dynamic campaign is a wonderful offense-defense based set of randomized missions in between which you prepare your unit composition. It feels more like each battle is a fresh skirmish, but with your veteran army you have built along the way.
Then of course, battles and skirmishes for both singleplayer and multiplayer.

[b]-Negatives-[/b]
Controls might feel a little clumsy and not immediately responsive, especially in third person direct control mode. This comes in the form of unpleasant "freezes" of your character or vehicle mid-animation, preventing any action for a brief moment. It is consistent enough, so you can likely get used to it.
Fog of war is slightly misleading, even though it feels like the more interesting way to play the game. Units tend to ignore it at times, shooting accurately without direct line of sight. This applies to both, your units and enemies. At times your men will shoot at enemy that you can not even see indicated on the map or in the field. 
There are still a few bugs, but all in all the fun this game offers easily outweights them.

This is on of the best RTS I've ever played. Amount of content is insane, I have 100+ hours on record and barely scratched the surface, mostly because I've been hooked up on dynamic campaign mode. But regular campaign missions are as good: they're diverse, they provide a challenge and many of them allow very different approaches adding to replayability. They also provide some of very unique scenarios that are underrepresented in WWII games like defending against the Red Army under Leningrad as spanish Blue Division or acting as a rear guard for the Red Army units retreating from Kerch peninsula, not to mention the whole Finland campaign.

Excessive attention to details like the full damage model for each vehicle including static weapons or ability to control individual units and tampering with their inventory provides a handful of tactical possibilities and greately contributes to the uniqueness of battles making each one a story in its own right. It also looks very cinematic and you truly feel like you're watching some good WWII movie with that amount of chaos and unexpected situations.

It's worth its money even when there's no sale. You'll also appreciate the friendliness to modding, absence of money-grabbing in form of in-game stores or microtransactions. It has DLC's, yes, but each one contributes to the game greately, adding a lot of new units, maps and singleplayer campaign missions.

Review of singleplayer: 

Price/Style of gameplay:

not for the price... hell no. The game is a moderate copy of assault squad 2 with better graphics. There's a 3rd person direct control mode, which is the only new thing compared to assault squad 2 in terms of new features. 

The missions seem kind of boring with the, here's 2 tanks, now go destroy the whole enemy army of 10000 men, style of gameplay.. 

I never liked that type of gameplay, from the previous men of war titles.

I always preferred playing big battles with the ability of a lot of reinforcements, so far I haven't ecnountered that in Gates of Hell.

AI:

The AI is crap, just like in every other comparable men of war style game.

Here's an example, the medics don't revive fallen soldiers, you have to micro-manage that... come on...  The units don't use cover properly, resulting in them all dying very fast to the enemy which makes the whole thing of limited amount of units for 1 battle completely useless. I need a lot of infantry that act as cannon fodder to go through trenches. You cannot rely on them doing the job properly on their own they don't know how to effectively use cover, they stroll around mindlessly and die to an enemy mg emplacement because instead of jumping for cover they act as if the mg wasn't even firing at them.. this lack of smart behavior just demonstrates how crazy outdated the AI of the engine is. 

Here's another example, while I'm playing the mission siege of Sevastopol. There are a huge amount of trenches and I'm only given a limited amount of units. My infantry gets depleted fast and dies. I'm given a small assortment consisting of 1x Stug, 1x panzer 3 and 1x panzer 4 along with 1x large artillery mortar, to destroy around 1000 enemy infantry, who are all well entrenched and have defensve positions with AT gun emplacements, mg nests etc. This battle could have been made so much more fun by just introducing reinforcements, more tank types, maybe fighter planes as support...

I could understand how for some people it might seem as a fun challenge, but to me it just feels boring, with me having to go into 3rd person in a singular tank and kill entrenched infantry 1 by 1 manually ESPECIALLY IF THE WHOLE BATTLE EVOLVES TO BE JUST THAT because you can forget sending units out on their own and expecting any positive results.

I wish the battle was more self-sustainable, as in, where you just right click and send units in a direction and they're able to actually utilize cover do advances on their own, move in smart patterns, medics who heal units, units who pick up ammo from a dead soldier next to them in order for them to resupply when they run out of ammo, ALL OF THIS without me having to 
 MANUALLY babysit them.. Then I could imagine that the 3rd person direct control would actually make sense because then I could actually feel immersed in the battle without having to worry about nonsense like resupplying a single soldier when I have like a 100 other soldiers that require the same attention...

The AI should be capable to do more on its own, come on it's 2023, not 2010...

Crashes / Problems:

The game crashes every now and then when I try to reload a saved game. 
I've also noticed while in 3rd person, if I'm in a trench the enemy has aimbot like precision and instantly kills. The collision inside a trench when clearing it is also weird. Imagine I'm in an L shaped trench, with the enemy on one end and me being on the other end inside 3rd person direct control. The enemy can with pinpoint precision shoot and kill me while they are prone.. through 10 meters of thick earth and mud...this just ruins the immersion, come on guys, this should've been done better... 

The camera is focused in a way so that when you're in 3rd person, you're viewing your soldier on the left side of your screen, there's no way to change that perspective, so that the soldier is on the right hand side of your screen, which caused me to die a bunch of times because I was forced to go around the whole trench, to shoot the enemy who was hiding. That's just ridiculous, camera controls aren't that hard to implement, something this simple should be in the game. 

The game also automatically assumes that I have a mouse with extra buttons which not everyone does. There should be a configuration for people who don't have extra buttons on their mouse but rather want to use their keyboard. Example is let's say, to make it easier to switch to a grenade while in 3rd person or a hotkey to switch grenade types or switch to a pistol from a rifle... in order to do any of those things I had to manually exit 3rd person and hover over the thing with the mouse... there should be hotkeys on the keyboard for this.

One more thing I noticed while using the 3rd person mode. The enemy AI shoots through obstacles. There is absolutely no regard to line of sight. They shoot you through a thick forest. This is just plain bad... How am I supposed to be immersed if the enemy shoots me with aimbot like precision through thick forests? What is even the point in 3rd person direct control then?

Overall:

It's a mess.. a lot of things could've been done better and should be improved for the price tag that they're asking for the DLCs and the game itself. All I can see as of right now is an overly glorified graphics mod for the original base game from 2009 men of war, with maybe slightly updated AI but it's not any better than, if for comparison, you gave a caveman a rifle and pointed him towards a ww2 battlefield.. the behavior of the AI is somewhat similar to that.

If you've read this, I sincerely hope that you, DO NOT think, I'm being harsh with this review. This game is not a standalone game. It requires you to purchase the base game Call to Arms itself in order to play it. It will cost 45 euros WITHOUT any additional DLCs. You want the DLCs for this "DLC game", add another 25 euros on top of that.... this is such an enormous price tag!!!!!!! FOR a game that is less than optimal, considering it's release in 2021 and 2023 standards and expectations. All the problems I mentioned above are legitimate and their existence is unjustified.

In many ways, comparing Ostfront to say, Company of Heroes, is quite alike comparing Battlefield to Call of Duty - both are great games, but take very different approaches in style and scale. Ostfront is far more of a simulation and goes to huge lengths to have its locations feel like real places, its units behave how you would in real life, and the moment-to-moment considerations feel more grounded in the setting than as a layer of abstraction. Thanks to its grand scale, ability to take direct control of units, and atmospheric presentation, you really feel like commanding over a real battle in a way that is rare for these kind of games.

Overall, Ostfront is a fantastic experience for anyone who enjoys deep, complex and engaging strategy games in a WW2 setting. It is extremely replayable and a huge amount of fun, only held back by its lack of polish in places and its vague presentation of how everything works. Both these are things that do keep improving and likely only will more so over time.

A very strong recommendation!

After almost 500 hours of playtime I can say that this game is definitely the king of the RTS genre at the moment. Here are some of the biggest points this game has to its name.

By far the biggest part of this game is micro. You need to focus on a a unit to put them into a good position but are also aware of all other units on the battlefield. This also means that there is always things to do but you can never get them all done, and you may miss big opportunities. This game is really for people who always want to be an active role in the battle and not as much for those who want to lay back and let the units do their thing. This is a pro and a con depending on your own play-style.

The second factor which might lead people towards and away from the game is realism. This is great as you get to experience the closest thing to a ww2 battle from a birds eye view. It also means that your units are not invincible. If you spend a bunch of points on a Tiger or IS-2, it can get taken out in an instant by a large AT-gun or infantry anti-tank weaponry.  There is always a risk for every unit. This will bring a lot of rage to the game but also satisfaction.

mods are important to keep many games fun and saturated. CTA GOH is no different. This does not mean that it is necessary for the game, but you will find that after a while, it gets repetitive.

Many people have noted how the AI is less than perfect... A lot less than perfect. This may cause players to rage as to why the supply trunk is driving in front of your tank or infantry taking the worst possible path. The dev team is trying to fix some of the issues related to AI, but it only means that you need to take a bit more care with your units. A little more management, but it is worth it.

Explosions...Just explosions. I like them. You will probably like them. Combined with destructible entities, it is incredibly satisfying.

The price is very high, way too high for what it is. but during steam sales, it drops by 75%. Take advantage of it!

There are many more points, some bad, lots of good, but in my opinion, it is the best around.

Hopefully the AI bugs are fixed in the future. I'll change my rating if they are.

Honestly? The best damn WW2 RTS I've ever played. Enjoying this one immensely and I don't even like RTS games that much in the first place.

It's hugely immersive and you can even control single units in 3rd person action game style. The attention to detail is one of the best I've seen in the genre and it's super fun with buddies online. 

The sounds are fantastic too. Even the units sound really good and they shout out useful things such as warning you about tanks, machine guns, when they need a medic or more ammo instead of just generic unit action blabber such as "Alright!" and "Copy!" provided you can understand the language that is.

The game is very micro heavy though. There are so many little things you can and often must do while you command the units, such as inventory management, first aid, reloading guns and keeping the gears of war well oiled. This is a non issue however as the game is more about intelligent troop positioning and pressing the advantage when it benefits you the most. A small handful of well positioned soldiers can deal a lot of damage to the enemy.

It can all get a little overwhelming occasionally and you'll likely get your ass handed back, but I find that losing is also quite fun. Something I rarely experience in regular RTS games, the few I've played. They just don't appeal to me at all, but this game for some odd reason does.

The biggest flaw I've noticed is perhaps the AI of your own troops. As I said, the game is pretty micro heavy and you need to babysit them a lot in certain situations and if that situation happens to be one where there is action all over the map, you're going to lose troops just because they can't save themselves.

Other than that it's a great game. Can't recommend it enough.

UPDATE: While some problems still persist, I'd say the devs have addressed a lot of the prior issues. Their mission design is still just... awful. It's common to get sniped by new enemies as you're cutscene-transitioned to new parts of it.

... so long as AI doesn't break again.

UPDATE: Mission design is just terrible. Compared to their work in Men of War, missions frequently give you vague objective descriptions. This means that you'll be preparing a defense for objectives without an understanding of where the enemy is actually coming from. You spend 15+ minutes setting up minefields and machine gun positions, only for the missions to go "Ha! Idiot! You should've guessed that the enemy would've been tank rushing from the South." It basically demands you either get some info on the forums or replay just to have a chance at enjoyably playing some of these missions.

Update mission descriptions and make the invasion attack arrows appear during defense setup stages.

EDIT: Infantry AI is unbelievably broken right now. They will forget to follow your commands or take a long time to comply. They'll barely shoot back and only seemingly under very specific circumstances. It's as if they're all stuck to Return Fire behaviour, more or less. This means you end up babying your frontlines a lot more, and coming back to other parts to find it blown to smithereens as you lost the initial trade of volleys. 

This is currently nigh-on non-functional and takes a great deal of the fun out of the game. Furthermore, click-dragging infantry squads into cover produces odd results that often just get them kill. 

Advancing requires constant Direct Control usage in order to have a hope in hell of hitting entrenched positions before they annihilate your helpless little ducklings. 

Finally, firefights have become deadly accurate. You barely need anyone to have snipers, as the first bullet out of an MG can sometimes laser through the enemy infantries heads with comical precision. We once had an enemy medic come around a corner and dome three of our men in the heads before any of them got a shot off. Funny, but too common.

The game in this state threatens to sour it for me and my friend, who have loved this game throughout all it's iterations, even given it's jankiness then.

P.S: Make ammo trucks replenish the equipped weapon, not the one they spawned with. It's just less fun. I don't care about immersion and realism here. It's already enough of a slog sometimes without this.
