[h1]Summary[/h1]
I want to recommend this game, but I can't in good conscious. There are so many little problems that are completely unacceptable for a real time tactics game that it just ruins the experience.

tl;dr There are a ton of bugs; bad gameplay mechanics; glitchy and poorly designed AI; and poor performance. I do not recommend Partisans 1941.

There are two distinct parts to this game: combat/tactics, and base-building.

[h1]Combat[/h1]
This is where the core of the game lies. You are a Russian partisan group behind enemy lines during the invasion of the Soviet Union in 1941. Your goal is to kill german soldiers and those that work with them (Polizei in the game). You also have missions around stealing information, blowing up bridges, etc.

[b]Pros[/b]
[list]
  [*]Stealth feels good. I haven't played that many really good stealth games, but I'd give it a 7/10. Not to say it's realistic or detailed, but it feels reasonably good to me. Arguably overpowered in some instances.
  [*]Lots of different gameplay styles. You can go full ninja, full Rambo, use grenades, distractions, and a bunch of other tools both in the environment and in your inventory.
  [*]Lots of different abilities you can choose from. Throwing knives, a slingshot to knock enemies out, precision rifle shot, AOE shooting abilities (SMG, pistol), and others. Some of them are arguably overpowered, but fun nonetheless.
[/list]

[b]Cons[/b]
[list]
  [*]The AI is dumb. REALLY dumb. Dumber that it should be for a modern game. There's no randomization in patrol routes & no change to behavior unless you enter combat. This makes it really easy to stealthily take out individuals or pairs and no one notices. tl;dr: the enemy AI runs on a loop and feels very rigid.
  [*]AI in combat is really bad. If you have one of your partisans off to the side trying to do something stealthy and is caught, EVERYONE is suddenly exposed and starts getting shot at. This happens no matter how far away your other partisans are.
  [*]Enemy soldiers are alerted instantaneously once combat occurs. If you lure someone into some bushes to knife them but in the millisecond before you do they notice you, everyone in the area is suddenly in combat and knows exactly where you are. Shooting combat is super frustrating because of this and the previous points.
  [*]Enemy soldiers are able to grab their weapons, aim them, and shoot at you instantaneously. There's no warm up, just instantly shooting.
  [*]The enemy vision range is explicit and has very hard edges. If you stand 1cm outside that range, even if you're in a completely open field in sunlight, they can't see you. It's kinda nice to be able to see the vision range, but it also really reduces the immersion and tension. I have an issue with the hard edges and short, unchanging distance.
  [*]Inventory management could use improvements. You can pick up random stuff during the mission that gives you food & supplies for your base. However, there isn't a nice way of organizing that stuff across your partisans in the mission. This makes inventory management very tedious in missions where you get a lot of extra stuff. If one of your partisans picks up a supply item and another partisan picks up the same supply item, you can't automatically combine them into a single stack between the two partisans. You have to manually move that item from one partisan to the other to stack them. I think stacking any of these items is a bad idea because you can have a bunch of singular items in your inventory that take up all of your space, yet you can still pick up more stuff but only if it's stuff you already have.
[/list]

Not sure:
[list]
  [*]There's an unrealistic behavior of the AI where if you engage in combat or something similarly loud (landmine, grenade, etc.) and there aren't any enemy soldiers within a certain range, no one else will hear it. This seems reasonable until you realize that range is nowhere remotely close to realistic. It's basically your fog of war distance. Maybe 30 yards? In real life, if an explosion happens down the street, you're going to notice it even if you didn't see it. If you're okay with that suspension of disbelief, then disregard this point. If you have trouble not thinking "why did no one just hear that landmine going off and killing 3 people?" then this will be bothersome to you.
  [*]Fog of war is super forgiving. You stand anywhere near a building and you can see inside it. Even if the side facing you has no windows. It's debatable on whether this is a pro or con.
[/list]

[h1]Base Building[/h1]
Between missions you go back to your base and can do things like:
[list]
  [*]Gather food
  [*]Collect supplies
  [*]Run missions that aren't controlled by you. Your partisans run off into the distance and there's a percentage chance they succeed. These missions give you XP and/or supplies.
  [*]Constructing buildings that will give you additional tasks you can do during your downtime
  [*]Upgrade weapons, make equipment, etc.
[/list]

[b]Pros[/b]
[list]
  [*]You can upgrade stuff between missions.
  [*]You can gain XP for your partisans between missions.
[/list]

[b]Cons[/b]
[list]
  [*]This part of the game is extremly shallow. You can build a few buildings and do a few things, but there's nothing meaningful about it. There's no ability to customize beyond what buildings you make.
  [*]You have to do tasks otherwise your partisans will have problems. You have to gather food frequently otherwise they starve.
  [*]Morale seems pretty much meaningless. Technically your morale can go down, but it seems difficult as long as your partisans don't starve.
  [*]Performance. Holy crap performance. Who built this part? It's completely unacceptable. When clicking on a button, it can take a half second for it to respond. During that time the entire game freezes. If you're looking at your inventory and you mouse between items in it, the entire game freezes for ~half a second each time you mouse between items. This is absolutely rediculous. Devs, if you're reading this, did you put a mutex on your entire game just to show some text in a rollover box? What the hell?
  [*]Looking through your skill tree unnecessarily limits you to seeing 5 of your partisans at the top of the screen. To see more, you have to scroll using the mouse wheel but that isn't obvious. I discovered it by accident. There's a ton of room at the top of the screen, why is it limited to only showing 5?
  [*]When your partisans run off to do their tasks, sometimes a couple of them just stand there next to the fire. The task is actually worked, but the partisan just stands there. Not really an "issue" in itself, but showcases the problems of this game. What other issues are hiding behind the scenes if something so obvious is in a fully released game?
[/list]

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
I really want to like this game. I have played RTT games on and off for a while and the setting for this one is fun. However, this is poorly implemented with lazy AI development and obvious problems with performance and bugs. The AI is far too rigid and doesn't include anything beyond "AI sees you". No object permanence, no change in routines, no background events, etc.

I will likely keep playing the game through because I can't return it at this point, but ultimately I do not recommend this game for others.

This game is similar to the other stealth strategies: Commandos, Desperados, Shadow Tactics. Unfortunately it doesn't come up anywhere near them.

There are very few games in this genre, so any new stealth experience is welcome.

The game is innovative in that it has a resource management system, you can even upgrade your weapons.

There is a lot of character banter in between the missions,

[h2]The cons[/h2]

The graphics is just plain bad. Even on a semi-high end machine it looks horrible - see some screenshots. I know this is generally a thing with Daedalic games, but still it's big con. [h2]Conclusion[/h2]

Why would you get this game? If you like the stealth strategy genre, just avoid this and instead go play Shadow Tactics or Desperados 3 again. Even though you've probably played it twice already, it will still be more fun than Partisans 1941.

This review was difficult, as I honestly love real-time strategy ever since playing the original Commandos. This game is an easy recommend for any fans of the genre who enjoy the old school tactics games. It's a much harder sell for literally anyone else.

The main issues I had:
- The folks making this game are really on to something with the mini basebuilding and character level ups going on. Unfortunately it's so shallow that it might almost not have been included at all. If made into a meaningful system that really feeds back into the missions, this would be really good. As things stand it's just more clicking you go through to get to the next mission.
- Having a bit stronger focus on action and not always having to avoid shootouts is a great idea. Unfortunately it's incredibly unbalanced. Additionally I feel that you either go full XCOM and turn your characters into disposable pieces on the chess board (would be so fitting for a war game!) or you make them a bit more balanced. I think Desperados or Shadow tactics got the character balance much better.
- Enemy behavious seems a bit weird at times. For example when you kill two enemies with a knife from the back and are just a split second off, everyone is alarmed immediately. This could be made so much better with a small grace period (again, Shadow Tactics and Desperados do that). On the other side you can literally kill a guard with a throwing knife from a bush and just run away unseen with enemies basically forgetting about the knife-throwing busches after about 30 seconds.
- It's impossible to see at a glance what range skills and items have. Please just give me a radius when I select a grenade or a throwing knife to see what my range looks like.
- Maybe I missed it in the tutorials but I missed a feature to mark a place in order to check if an enemy can see that. The original Commandos even had that and I feel it's necessary.
- Some verticality would have been awesome. I don't mind sneeking around forests and farmsteads or through enemy controlled train stations, but please at least let me get my sniper up into a snipers nest on a barn roof or allow some of my characters to climb up some vines into a window or something. This was a feature Commandos 2 had more than a decade ago.
- The game still feels a bit glitchy at times. It's unfortunate, since you really have to save every 10 seconds in case something happens.

Despite all of this I still played the game from start to finish, but I don't think I'll ever circle back to it in the same way I do with Shadow Tactics or Desperados. It's such a shame as I love the genre and really appreciate the effort. I just don't think that this game is really good for anyone but the ones who can look beyond its flaws and missed chances.

entertaining for the first half and then the game disregards all the strategic team building you did and tells you which troops are going on missions. Inventory management is annoying. Stealth gets difficult with more than 2 enemies on the screen as you can only see one vision cone at a time and you may get detected even if outside of it. Better tactical games exist.

I saw this game on Steam a long time ago but I was kinda afraid to try it because of all those reviews mentioning numerous bugs. But finally I gave it a try using a "trial" version. 
Suddenly the game turned out to be so good that I bought the most expensive edition (on sale, but still). I recalled my teenage years in 1999 when I played the first Commandos and dreamt how cool it would be to have Commandos on the Eastern Front. The game is virtually my childhood dream that allows me to be a war hero I always wanted to be reading books and watching movies about the Great Patriotic War.
I don't know how foreigners perceive this game (I'm Russian and I play in Russian) but for a Soviet-born person it feels fantastic.
The Characters do not seem to be very responsive, for example when double clicking , running doesnt take effect unless you double click multiple times. the graphics is great. remind me of Commandos

Just approaching end of the campaign, but I have to say this game has been fantastic. Would recommend it to anyone that loves these kind of tactical action games with huge stealth elements to it.

Starting from playable characters. All of them have their own little backstory that makes them interesting and not just some random Partisan that joined you. Also each of them has their own unique abilities that makes them more valuable in certain situations, thus allowing you to build team compositions for missions in the way you want (with few mission exceptions). If you want full stealth, well why not? it's very much possible. All out attack? sure, just take characters that focus on guns. 

In general gameplay is really good. As mentioned before, game gives you a lot of freedom to do missions in few different ways, and that really allows every character to shine. I've mostly focused on stealth myself since it's really fun, but you can do it in your own way. Gunplay is realistic in a way that weapon choice really matters depending on the situation, and distance is so so important. Smart positioning is also key. Enemies have quite a smart AI and won't be fooled too easily, so you have to play your actions nicely. They also make use of explosives and mines, just as you do, and have dogs to find you in hiding spots, which is a cool little detail.

Between the missions you are at your base chilling and making plans about the future missions. Game always provides random dialogues there so you can learn a thing or two about characters and their story, as well about what's going on in Russian during those months. There's missions you co do while at base too, that reward you with resources, food and equipment. Nothing groundbreaking but gives you something to do at least.

My main gripe with the game is the fact that in some situations, lack of keybinds shown, especially in base. So you have to use your mouse to navigate, select and then exit again. Kinda weird that but cause rest of the game is really good, I can look past it.

This game is sort of like if Desperados III and XCOM had a premature baby. You're about to read a lot of complaints, but I did enjoy this game quite a bit.

This game is a buggy and unpolished mess. I played through on normal, and the bugs were so numerous and frequent that I think I might have smashed my monitor to pieces if I had been playing on the hardest difficulty (where you can't save during tactical missions). The most prominent bugs for me were: 1. The game struggled to constrain the mouse cursor within the game window, so the cursor would constantly fly off to another monitor. I could temporarily fix this by pausing the game, but the bug would consistently return a few minutes later. 2. Characters will occasionally get permanently stuck on objects like boxes and walls. If this happens to one of your partisans, it almost always requires loading a save as most missions can only be finished by moving your entire squad to a specific area on the map. If a a Nazi gets stuck on something, it will cause them to sort of phase out of existence and become untargetable by most weapons and abilities. The only methods I've found to correct this situation is to intentionally run into the stuck NPC's view cone, or to spend a usage of an AOE kill ability (like Massacre). Either of these bugs occurring on the hardest difficulty is likely to force a full mission restart.

The game also generally runs pretty poorly for no clear reason. 


There's also a huge list of bizarre design choices such as:

Completely randomized loot on most enemies and boxes.

Vague or sometimes inaccurate descriptions for skill tree abilities (this seems at least partially due to the somewhat lazy English translation).

Some skills are borderline useless (Strength, Inspiration II) while others are completely overpowered (Whistle II, Body Shield).

Not allowed to drop food / supply items after picking them up.

Partisans that can specialize in rifles are generally far better in combat than other partisans. 

The economy and progressions systems feel very off. Everything that costs supplies feels insanely expensive, and the utility of many base buildings is questionable at best. There's also no explanation for what a building does or how it works until you build it. 


Despite all these issues, I enjoyed this game. There aren't a lot of serviceable games like this, so I'm willing to accept a considerable amount of jank. If you enjoyed Desperados III / Shadow Tactics, this might scratch that sort of itch, but it's definitely nowhere near as satisfying.

This game is a good Commandos clone, but a bit more forgiving, as you can shoot your way out of the encounters in case things go wrong. The characters aren't as unique as I would like, but each one has a useful skill, and can specialize in some of the weapon types, which will turn them into great killing machines. I had only two crashes and some minor bugs during my time. The graphics seem a bit weird at first, and I recommend turning sharpening off as it makes the environment look worse.

Great Real time Tactical game. So far in my experience with the game it would seem you can go completely stealthy in every mission. Some are a little more challenging than others at remaining hidden. While others are just a patience game. I assume I'll come across a mission that does not allow me to be stealthy, but so far it is very fun being able to stealth kill and hide the bodies. Almost as if I am playing a top down Hitman game set in WW2. 10/10 Recommend.

Most difficult game I've played in a long time.... 

Most people reading this are either from Humble Bundle, or a fan of RTS- so two audiences, only one of which I'm a part of.

I abhor RTS games, X-Com games, 4X, whatever the hell genre this game is... Controlling multiple characters at the same time, each with "unique" abilities, etc... 

Stealth is the name of the game... It should be Tom Clancy's PartiCell 1941... 

I'm on the..... 3rd?? Mission of the game? After 6 hours of playing... And dying..  And playing, and getting spotted, and playing and getting spotted, and quicksaving after every single stealth takedown I make when I remember to which unfortunately is VERY RARELY... 

So the game is generous with saves, unless you're on the hardest difficulty, in which case you can't save.. I'm on THE EASIEST difficulty and there's something "off" about the enemy placement...

Every level feels like it's setup in AN INCREDIBLY specific way, with a specific path to take, masquerading as a game you can make infinite choices in... Quickly you will realize you have NO FREEDOM, until I assume later in the game when you can finally craft different things that will help.... Well for my first six hours I've been wandering bush to bush, placing a non-infinite amount of bottles on the ground, throwing a rock, luring one guard away from 3 to an area that looks like a vision dead zone only to realize, "Nope, that one guard literally across the camp turns his head at such an unfortunate time, while another one looks at the exact same spot the second the other turns his head away... Ok, so... Can't do that...

It's a puzzle game of trial and error... Which guard do the devs want me to take out next, and WHAT do I have to do to get him out of the line of sight of quite literally 7 other guards, scattered across the camp, whose vision cones are sweeping across the entire camp, (and your planned target) incessantly.. 

It's also all in Russian with subtitles..... This is not a game who's story I care about, it's NOT INTERESTING, it's INCREDIBLY cliche so far, but again, I'm only on Mission 3, I've just been playing with the same 3 characters the ENTIRE time.. The dialogue is beyond sub-par... ANY of the characters you meet/play as/control could die in the story and I wouldn't even think twice... Even the chipper young enthusiastic, "I wanna face the world" 14 year old kid who's immediately on your team. I actually DO hope he gets killed off, that's how unsatisfying his interactions are... Main protagonist "badass" is too generic to even be worth discussing.. He's the Commander of a former something in the Soviet Union, it truly doesn't matter at all.. 

Ok so the story is terrible, the dialogue in general is hair-pulling... Music? Well, there isn't really any gameplay soundtrack, so that's not worth mentioning....

What else? I can't say.. I would like to give more insight into what the game has to offer, but after more than 6 hours, and such a slow burn, I can neither recommend this nor discourage, so I'm going to give the benefit of the doubt towards people who like these types of games. If you think 6 hours of studying patrol patterns and struggling to work your way through, (not joking) 30 Germans with a knife, and if you're spotted you immediately fail and go back to the last save point- (which could be the beginning of the level multiple times if you're like me.... At some point you just start speedrunning the damned missions because you're so fed up, which leads to more mistakes, which ultimately leads to an Alt-F4 after a few good hours..) If all that sounds frustrating and NOT your cup of tea, I'd stay away...

If you have more experience controlling multiple incredibly vulnerable characters through swarms of enemies without being alerted, yet still needing to kill them through the use of the same exact way of luring them with a shiny bottle of rum they all say "It must be my Lucky Day!" when they spot and walk over to it, by throwing a rock to get their attention to look towards, and then stealth killing them from a bush like you did to the last 10- if this is your genre, you may have fun with this... 

The atmosphere is good. I like the period. I like the idea behind the game... So even after what seems like a scathing review, the passionate anger and hatred I feel for this game kinda makes me want to keep playing and see if your characters EVER become viable, or if you're CONSTANTLY in a state of glorified Puzzle solving.. You can craft different items, I just built the workshop at your camp you fix up.... But after a couple nights (one of which is dedicated to healing injuries and food) you're forced to go on a mission when all ya really wanna do is a random Task that came in that gives you supplies and XP. Overnight... But no you needed to heal and fish. And now you gotta go do a mission that takes, in my case, and I can't help but imagine many others also, roughly 2 hours to finish... 

It's not as chill of a game as I'd thought... I would have liked very little brain work, but alas that's not the case... And the fact that I can't listen to the story, I have to read subtitles of the characters speaking Russian is also INCREDIBLY annoying.. The story is already so uninteresting, at least let me check my phone... Why does it take Russians 25 seconds to say "The Fascists have a tank. Blow it up.." Ok, so after reading that, can you skip thru phrases like Fallout, or Pokemon, or literally any other game with dialogue? No but you can hold space and skip the ENTIRE dialogue, which at the end of the day, seems less and less like you're missing out on ANYTHING of value.. 

I'm going to beat this 3rd mission.... I may even move on to the 4th mission... After Mission 4, I will have about 10-15 hours in the game, and I may update my review accordingly. 

If this isn't your genre, do not buy it.. If you like X-Com style games, I'd read a different review from someone qualified in the genre... If you received it in your HB like myself, and you're wondering whether it's worth booting up..... That's why I have to leave a Thumbs Up.. It's worth booting up to see if it's for you. 

Some games you play and they just aren't for you.. Some games you play and you realize "This is a BAD GAME, and the majority of sane people will ALSO think this is a terrible game.." Others leave you feeling confused yet open to the idea that there could be an audience for this.. This game is the latter for me...

I can't help but feel like this is a good game for the right people, and an "okay" game for someone to try out who's not big on awkward camera angles and games anywhere under the genre of "Strategy." 

Feel free to comment, check me, correct me, and even give pointers if you think there's something I'm obviously missing in terms of being successful.. I could CERTAINLY use them.. 

But if you disagree that Sanek is the most annoying "Side-Protagonist" in any game you can imagine to date, I'll probably disable comments because I want the conversation to be fruitful, not full of sociopaths. And if you think Sanek is charming, you're unstable, and very likely *dangerous* like a *rattlesnake..*

This is one of those games that you'd give a "mixed" review.

Partisans strives to be like Commandos, Desperados or even Shadow Tactics (which is from the same publisher incidentally), which are the pinnacle in this genre.
However, it fails to achieve this level of greatness, yet it's still fun to play through for the most part.

The main meat of the game are of course the missions, 15 in total (+ some standalone missions if you want to). In between you will "manage your base", which is nothing to really highlight. You have to gather food and supplies, raid enemy encampments automatically to get weapons and ammo, craft basic explosives, etc.

Each partisan you gather during your playthrough has his or her own skill tree, is better with certain weapons, better at stealth or just a mean killing machine.

Gameplay, however, revolves around stealth for the most part. You CAN go in guns blazing, but that's risky, since alarming one guard often alarms the entire map, meaning you have to contend with 50+ enemies, and you're just going to be outgunned, even with heavy weapons and grenades. Your partisans will also get injured (they can't die, unless all of them die). Since ammo is rather scarce this isn't the preferred way of playing the game, but sometimes open conflict is unavoidable, so cover is important, since it reduces the chance to be hit by a lot. Especially SMGs are totally useless in these sort of situations though, since you'll just burn through ammo without hitting anything.

I'd always favour the dedicated melee characters, with which you can lure enemies and take them out rather easily. Unless the enemy AI just decides to not give a ♥♥♥♥ about it. This game follows a very peculiar design choice, in which enemies will not always follow set paths, but do whatever they want. This is especially noticeable when you load a quick save and realize the enemy has done something completely different than last time ... or that time has skipped forward 2 to 3 seconds for no apparent reason (I can only explain this by believing the game isn't synced with the actual loading times). This leads to you doing the exact same thing with wildly different outcomes. Especially terrible are the "don't get spotted" missions, where it's sometimes enough for an isolated enemy to see you for a fraction of a second before he dies. You have to time your kills absolute perfectly, unless you want the whole camp to be alerted. To make it short: There is a disconnect between what is happening on screen and what is happening behind closed curtains. Also, screw the dogs.

The AI has another problem though. It's just plain stupid. I've had enemies see a corpse, freak out and immedietaly know where I am, despite having no way of knowing where I am. In other instances they didn't find me at all, despite a dog literally standing 1 feet away from me and having me sniffed out, only to completely freak out again when they "discover" the corpse AGAIN (happened after a load ... you'd think they'd at least remove the body or that they'd stay alert forever). I've also had enemies just not react to my lures ... enemies that suddenly turn around though they've never done that before ... and enemies that just run into a wall, all agitated, only for me to kill them all in bewilderment with 1 of my guys, who can kill several at once.

Level layout is generally good, but missions always end up being played the same way: Sneak from bush to bush and kill isolated enemies. In Shadow Tactics for example you have different characters that can fulfill different roles, in Partisans I often needed 2 guys to do the job 1 guy should be able to. I've also frequently had commands not register and my guys generally doing whatever they wanted.

Atmosphere and the, I guess, original Russian language is superb though, even the German Russian accents. Most of it is flawless, which considering Daedalic is a German company I'd expect (when it comes to German). Overall a pretty decent game for the asking price. But nothing you will play more than once.

I finished campaign and after that didn't wanted to even review it. It took me around 23 hours so, in its time its medium length game, but it got ruined by its story and game mechanics itself. 
Sure its not trash game, but I came with high expectation and got very disappointed.

7 enemy soldiers are left. One has a patrol route that takes him a bit away from the others. I sneak one of my partisans up and dispatch him with a quick knife in the back. Removing his field of vision allows another partisan to take out a guard with a bit of chloroform. With 5 enemies left, I move my partisans into a position surrounding them, ensuring the enemy will be unable to take cover. My shotgun fighter takes the first shot, removing two enemies quickly. But if you liked Commandos, you will definetly like this!
Meh, it's basically a remake of an old WWII saboteur game that I forgot the name of, but as I recall, the old one was better (or maybe I'm just being nostalgic)

First, in case you were curious - the developer of this game is not mimimi (so the game is not as perfect as you may expect.)

It's the same publisher as the shadow tactics and desperados 3, yes. So the genre is about right.

It will take some time to get used to its engine, and it's not really as hand held as it should.

There will be realy clutz moments where you think you can do something but the character will refuse (because he's busy).

Or you strap up one of your new recruits with precious mines and grenades, only to see him leave the mission half way thru, due to the screenplay plot.

One particular missing feature is that you cannot click on an empty ground to see who's watching that spot. You have to actually click on the characters.

Once, I ran into a situation where I could not finish a level at all - the finish marker would not show up, even though I completed all of the objectives (about the 7th or 8th mission with the mill and poison). Killed everyone including dogs and civilians. Ended up blowing up everything. After restarting the entire campaign (not the mission!) from scratch - the bug went away.

Most of the levels are stealth, but there is one surprise mission where you'll have to sweat and swear over a machine gun! Loved and hated it lol.

Overall a pretty enjoyable and thorough game, that took well over 50 hours to beat and master.

In short it´s more combat and narrative oriented 3D Commandos in Russian. 

The Eastern Front - and especially the partisan efforts against operation Barbarossa aren´t usually the scenarios that are depicted in video games and that worked great as a backdrop for the game and the building of your troops and equipment and the plot through the campaign felt realistic enough. The main difference to Commandos (I don´t think you can talk about this game without mentioning Commandos) is that has a real plot and real characters - even though you probably end up using 3-4 same characters over and over.

As a Finn it was interesting to see the Finnish portrayed as the evil Axis who perish in the hands of partisans of Karelia and the main character is said to have risen in his rank in the Finnish/Winter War. 

All in all a pretty good game with, most of complaints I can think of are of the game stability and towards the end I was keeping my fingers crossed it won´t brake before the end. Also the base building part seemed too bare boned and I´m not sure if the food count worked properly. Maybe some balancing could be done as you can only choose 3 partisans per mission and most of them just end up sitting in the camp. I don´t think chose the medic even once. 

Towards the end your characters become pretty much terminators and you can decimate legions of nazis with ease if you just have enough grenades and mines and the only thing stopping total carnage is lack of ammunition. Speaking of carnage - there should have been more gore in my taste to make the war hell. 

If you like real time tactics, guerilla warfare and world war 2 I highly recommend to give it a shot.

One of the clunkiest games I am giving a positive review for I was sucked in for all 40 hours of the campaign (most people probably will be able to finish it in 20 hours or less). It has many issues, it is not polished, but it captivated me and worked like time machine - just one more mission I wanted to play and 4 more hours passed.. and then again and it was 11 am in the morning. I recommend when on sale. 

What I liked about the game:
- The setting, the theme
- The story
- The music
- The trivia about russian partizan and war heroes
- non-linear missions - you have many options how to approach each enemy, you can and don't have to kill all enemies, you can select any weapons or partizans for the mission you like

Some of the many issues:
- wonky graphics, e.g. shots with 90% chance to hit fired few meters wide graphically, but they still hit the enemy - happens all the time
- weird cover mechanics with spots - if you are behind wall but not on the spot, you're dead even if it looks you're better covered than other partizan just near you on the spot... and there is an issue with possibility of having 2 or even 3 partizans over each other on the same cover spot, which looks a graphical bug and it seems only one of them is being covered.
- stupid AI, especially when searching for you and they don't care about missing buddies, even when on spot they never should've left - like machine gun nests.. or you kill their dog and after a while the group happily walks the same path again..

Fun game if very short. Buy on a sale and it's probably worth it. 

Pro tip - the DLC does not extend the game it adds extra skirmish missions so it's not worth buying.

It's a great game. I bought it in Humble Choice, thinking I could try it at least, and so far I like it more than the game I picked the Choice for (Endzone). I like strategy games, but I'm more of a turn-based kind of player. I like XCOM a lot, but I'm not the biggest fan of Commandos-style games (even though I played Commandos 2 back in the day). 

But this was a pleasant surprise. Stealth is required in some missions, but not mandatory in most of them. The stealth parts of the game are fun (although be prepared to replace your F5 and F9 keys of your keyboard, I cannot bring myself to play Ironman in these kind of games, unlike I do with turn-based strategy games). And the shootings are pretty good: if you're a good planner, you can ambush your enemies, encircle them and end the fight before they notice you're there. If you do it badly, the enemies will take cover, throw granades and try to flank you, and before you notice, your partisans will be dying.

The story is not bad, although it's nothing special either. You're a partisan, doing guerilla stuff behind enemy lines. The Germans are the bad guys, so be prepared to hate them (your characters are defending their homeland, so don't expect sympathetic German characters or any of the sort. It's a Russian game, about people defending Russia in the war, and obviously the enemy is a faceless murderer you need to kill before he kills your people; it's not objective, but it's not supposed to be). The story also doesn't contradict the gameplay, you're a small group and take care of small operations; no character talks about how little resources you have when in reality you have a small arsenal of captured weapons and ammunition or things like that.

The characters are not too bad and even though they're pretty one-dimensional, you can tell them apart and recognise their main traits (Fetisov is an optimist, good-natured and idealistic; Belozerova is also idealistic but more fanatic and asertive; Trofim is a cynic who has seen all, Zorin is a cool-headed guy, a career officer with war experience...). You don't go deep into their backstories, they don't have an arc, but that fits this kind of game. Also, there are collectibles like pictures of Pravda articles to show you little stories from the war, so that's nice. The only think I don't like is there are not swastikas in the flags and there is no word "nazi" in their vocabulary. I understand developers don't want to deal with idiotic laws and want to sell their game, specially small studios who cannot afford lawsuits. I understand that, but I cannot avoid feeling History being erased from our popular culture. If there is a context where that word should be used and that logo should be show is this one.

The levels are nice, most missions are not too long, the graphics are okay (I'm not a guy cares a lot about graphics), the music is okay and the acting is pretty good (I like the Russians speaking in Russian, and the Germans speaking in German).

In conclussion, I usually write reviews after I've completed the game, and even though I'm not done yet, I'm confident I can recommend this game. If you're in the fence and it's on sale, don't think about it, because it's a good game and worth a buy.

P.S. Improve Zorin's knife throwing ability and Fetisov's SMG "I kill EVERYONE in fron of me" ability as soon as you can.

I haven't had this much fun playing a game on my own for years. Great story and good gameplay. There are some kinks here and there but mostly it is a smooth run. I look forward to more games like this!

Fairly enjoyable game overall. Quick loading times, unique gameplay, buildings with interiors. All done very well. But it feels like this is an alpha version and they just decided to stop working on it.

Issues and bugs:
- I want to move a group of partisans next to a house, so I click next to the house. The game then decides that half the group should move INSIDE the house. They are killed as they move around the house to find a doorway.
- I want to move a partisan behind a fence, but the camera is rotated in such a way that the fence blocks the view to that location. So (as with any other game) I pretend for a moment that the fence is hidden and click at the desired location. The partisan does not move at all. I cannot move there without rotating the camera.
- I want to move a piece of equipment from one soldier to another, so (as with any other game) I click/drag the item, then select another soldier with the number key, then release the click. No item is moved and the original soldier is selected again. I've also had a pistol duped and other items disappear while trying to move items.
- When there are multiple dead soldiers I end up picking up corpses when I wanted to loot due to the controls. 
- The controls cannot be changed. They can be viewed in the settings but not changed at all.
- Loot is RNG. That enemy rifleman carries neither rifle nor ammo. Or maybe 2 shotgun rounds. Camp management also has RNG.
- While the game communicates chance to hit, there is no enemy health indicator. Will my rifle kill that enemy with one hit? No idea. Guess I will save and reload if necessary.
- I shoot and kill a single enemy in front of an enemy camp, then run away. The rest of the camp instantly enters combat. No matter where I move (while always out of sight of the enemy), the enemy soldiers know exactly where I am and chase me around the entire map.

When tabbing out of the game, the GPU power draw increases to 100% instead of going down. GPU memory usage is oscillating and spends 10 s to slightly increase and then 10 s to slightly decrease in a sawtooth pattern. Highly dubious.

- The Mosin rifle does not seem to be part of random drops, so the highest level version cannot be obtained.
- Shotguns have some delay before firing, so if an enemy rifleman runs around a corner right into your line of sight, he will always have the first shot and most likely kill you.
- The buckshot ability works through walls.

Slightly glitchy, but loads of fun despite that.  It's one of the better games of this type, similar to to the Commandos, Desperados, or Shadow Tactics series, but there's fewer character limitations.  For example, several characters can use a knife, everyone can set and disarm traps, anyone can use any weapon, etc.  Some are definitely better than others, and some have very specific advantages.  One can throw knives (useful for killing silently at a distance), another can distract the enemy, one has a sniper skill (as opposed to just using a rifle), etc.

The history documents you run into are fun, and the atmosphere is very enjoyable as well.  The missions are pretty varied in scope and type, and while you can use almost any partisan(s) for any missions, there are certainly times when it's obvious that some are better suited for that particular mission.  You can never have enough mines, btw.

There are times when I'm not sure if the game was glitching or specifically designed that way.  I'd take my partisans down one path, run into a group of enemies, die, have to reload, then go a different way and find that the enemies were now following a different path, almost anticipating my new approach.  In the other games I mentioned, the enemies always follow a specific path.  If the guards followed a path once, they followed it every time.  In Partisans, that's not always the case, and if it was an intentional design approach, I think it was brilliant.

There *are* glitches, though; especially with concealment.  Concealment isn't always effective, and you'll find that you're hiding in a bush and the enemy's sight cone clearly shows that you aren't visible, but his alert meter still fills up and he spots you.  Reload the game, though, and suddenly his alert meter acts the way it should.  This happens often enough that I found myself saving on a pretty regular basis.

Some of the really enjoyable missions were ones where I'd lay down mines in multiple areas, then shoot a bad guy and immediately retreat to hiding somewhere, just to wait for the mines going off and dozens of bad guys getting blown up.  There's one particular mission, set in a rail yard, with an air raid you call in at the end, and you find dozens and dozens of bad guys coming after you.  Prior to that, I found myself swimming in ammo, but by the end of that, I was almost tapped out, and I was sweating throughout.  It didn't help that you can't save the game during that stage, but that also made it more fun.

Some general tips:
- Mines are AWESOME.  Get a workshop ASAP and always be building more.  Also, if you find yourself in a mission with a minefield, restart it if needed and bring a guy who can grab those mines.
- Stealth is awesome, but always loot as much ammo as you can.  You'll need it, eventually.
- I didn't realize it right away, but the overall skill level of your partisans directly impacts their chances of succeeding at the missions on the daily screen (between the main missions).

Great real time tactics/strategy/rpg game.

Essentially the game is split into two. There's the main game: you command your partisans to sneak, stab, shoot, ambush, distract, bomb, explode, misdirect, etc. For this mission you (usually) pick up to 3 partisans (although the commander is always part of the battle, so really you only pick two). Each partisan is somewhat unique with unique skills, abilities, etc that you unlock with exp your team earns through kills, completing objectives, etc. Note: if any of your team mates are spotted then your entire team will shoot at whatever enemies are near them. So if one person is spotted, your team mates hiding in bushes but behind zero cover might accidentally get themselves naded/shot to death. That being said I loved playing this game, especially trying to find creative ways to unalive every single enemy on a map.

on your team of partisans you get:
You got the expert doctor who is also a sniper, the old man living in the woods with his shotguns and traps, the star athlete than can operate machine guns and sub machine guns very effectively, the kid who is also a master of disguise/ knocking people out, the sketchy commissar who stabs and uses enemies as human shields, etc.

While on mission you also scavenge for supplies. Your ammo/ weapons are limited by what you find on the field of battle and on side missions at home base (more on that later) and every character has a limited backpack space (although for the most part with careful inventory management you can usually carry nearly everything you find on a battlefield).

Between battles you manage your partisan camp. This mostly consists of selecting construction projects, assigning partisans to do household chores/gather food, etc. You can also send them on side missions. These side missions will have a description like "raid the truck convoy", "propaganda", etc. You have a likelihood of success on this missions written as a percentage and higher level partisans increase this percent. These side missions are automatically played out and usually reward you with ammo, supplies, explosives, higher tier guns, etc that you can then bring with you on missions.

There's also a morale mechanic that's never fully explained in the tutorials:  if your team has a higher morale they do everything faster and better: abilities, shooting, etc. You gain morale from some specific side missions and you lose morale when you rob supplies from the local population (items that are in red when you scavenge). 


That being said, I really enjoyed playing the game. Its a neat concept, would be cool to see how they could improve upon it. I really wish they used this concept in other types of settings. Highly recommend.

One of my all time favourite games. Period. I knew I would like this game the moment I was introduced to it and its' concept. 

When I first played it I fell in love. There is so much about this game I could rant about, so I will.

[h1] The Concept [/h1]
Conceptually I love this game. I have always had a love for media around Partisans, what little there is. So any work that shines light on this under-explored topic gets an immediate win in my book. 

[h1] The Gameplay [/h1]
Partisans 1941, makes me feel like a partisan. Some people don't like the resource management, I can understand that, but I am not one of those people. I love the feeling of accruing weapons and materials for my partisans. Finding ways to conserve my resources while still getting as much use as possible. The Inventory UI is quite the mess though. I do hope if Alter have any plans to continue support for Partisans 1941, that they rework it. 

The tactical and stealth aspects of the game are really well done and fun; however I do have some complaints. The time delay between an enemy spotting you and them bursting to action is far too unforgiving. 

I don't want it to be too forgiving, because then it wouldn't be as challenging. The challenge of this game is a large part of the fun for me. Now admittedly this isn't too big of a problem in most missions; except stealth only missions, where if you don't [b] instantly [/b] deal with the target who saw you then it's game over. On hard this can make stealth missions agonizingly tedious as you run through the same guards to get back to the point you were previously at, over, and over. 

Outside of stealth only missions however I don't find this too much of an issue, as you are usually able to eliminate a target before they can sound any alarms. 

[h1] Difficulty [/h1]
I touched on this before, but the difficulty of this game is one of my favourite aspects. This game can be [b] difficult [/b] on hard. Perfect coordination and planning between your characters is required. It is punishing; without feeling undeserved. When I get a mission fail, it's [i] almost [/i] always because I mess up. 

I would genuinely recommend that players looking for the proper Partisans 1941 experience play on hard. On normal I was enjoying the game. On hard; I was [b] loving [/b] it. On hard, your Partisans are F*cked if you don't use proper positioning. On normal I was able to savescum my way to perfect stealth runs, where I only used melee and stealth abilities. Hard made me realise that a properly set up ambush is not only more effective at times, but more [i] fun. [/i]

[h1] Style and Graphics [/h1]
Partisans is a pretty intensive game, my rig can run it relatively well, but on some of the bigger maps with lots of enemies, I will find frame rate drops. I don't hold this too much against the game however; because the resulting artwork and style of the environments, characters, and enemies is work every lost frame to me. Would I take a better optimised game? In a heart beat. Would I take it at the expense of the games graphics? Probably not. 

If you own the art book for this game, and have looked at it, you will understand the care put into the creation of the environments. Not just from a level design aspect, but also the care put into the design of buildings to make them as immersive and accurate to the setting as possible. 

The one area I find the Graphics lacking is in the character models, even on the highest settings the characters are weirdly blurry and hard to make out. Which is a shame because I rather like the characters. speaking of. 

[h1] Characters [/h1]
The characters are an area I think are rarely spoken of in this game. Possibly because it's not exactly what you come to an RTT game for, but I find that the personalities of the characters all shine through without becoming shallow and one-note. 

The writers managed to make each character feel rather distinct without falling to just making simple character quirks and playing them up. Show me a character from this game and I could describe their personalities to you, because they stick out to me that well. However that may be saying more about me admittedly.

[h1] sound track [/h1]
Another underappreciated aspect of the game, Vladislav Isaev and Elena Isaeva did a wonderful job on this score. It's one you likely won't notice, especially if you play on low volume or with music off. As someone who owns the soundtrack however I must say it is so atmospheric and immersive. It reminds me a lot of Halo ODSTs soundtrack. Give it a listen if you have it.

[h1] Conclusion [/h1]
All-in-all, I think Partisans 1941 is a brilliant game. One of my favourites of all time. It is one of two games I have bought the Supporter pack for. The other being Barotrauma. I do not regret a single dollar. Quite the opposite, if I had, had the money, I would have bought this game at full price instead of on sale. Seeing as I did not however, I am glad I bought this game, and its' extended edition.

It's a good title. Obviously close thematically to Commandos, though it differs in that Partisans is not wholly stealth based like similar tactical RTS games. Setting up ambushes or brief skirmishes out in the open are also part and parcel of the game. There is also a degree of resource/base management, where you allocate resources to build and maintain your hideout. Hidden items from cabinets or officers, which contain historical tidbits from the Eastern Front was a nice touch.

The only downside is that the user interface is pretty rough around the edges: the cursor element for cover positions tend to interfere with fine-tuned positioning on items like bottles as lures. The cluttering of resource items / ammunition does also get a bit frustrating; loot items that contribute to the camp resources but have no other use take too much space in the inventory, crowding out the already highly-differentiated ammunition et cetera somewhat adversely influence gameplay.

The learning curve is pretty straightforward. Prior to the start of the mission you need to review the map and plan your strategy. There's no tutorial on how to manage your crew and improve your base in between missions other than viewing Youtube videos. There are path finding issues. PARTISANS 1941  is similar to Commandos. Overall, I 'm enjoying the experience. I'd give the game a 7.5 out of 10.

[h1]A surprisingly good modern iteration of the Commandos formula, Partisans 1941 is as solid an RTS as you can get[/h1] 

When commander Zorin and his subordinate Fetisov manage to escape a POW camp in the opening days of the Eastern Front and embark on a journey of resistance, little did they know that they were laying the foundations of a veritable partisan cell. What initially amounted to a struggle for survival and hopefully getting to know about the state of the war ended up in evolving into makeshift reprisal against the invaders and eventually, coordinated retaliation against the occupiers. It is a tale that seeks to embody the experience of resistance in the occupied Soviet Union throughout the lens of a made-up partisan cell that, however, is inspired in the real-life feats and experiences of partisans in the war. This is delivered in the form of an isometric RTS, much like Commandos, which puts you in the shoes of this band of resistance fighters bent on thwarting the conqueror's advance into their land.

This partisan cell, comprised of an ever-growing cast of characters that join your ranks the more you progress in the story, gathers around a forest encampment which you can buiild, enhance and from where you can plan your next step. When not in a mission, this makeshift encampment is your HQ, where you may take inventory of items in your storage, send members on off-screen missions to gather resources (you have to feed and heal your partisans) and XP, which they use to level up. This is where you will spend most of the time between main missions and serves as a relief of sorts after tense levels.

And speaking of missions: Partisans borrows heavily from Commandos, and rightly so: Commandos defined an era in isometric RTS-gaming. But whereas Commandos relies heavily on stealth and tip-toeing around enemy patrols, Partisans is all about positioning your soldiers behind cover, awaiting for the precise moment to strike an unwary patrol. Whereas Commandos emphasises avoiding large-scale pitched battles, Partisans compels you to engage in them. For whereas commandos in real life dealt with espionage, information theft and such, Partisans dealt primarily with sabotage and ambushes, so while at first glance one might be tempted to draw parallels between them, there is a stark difference at heart, and that is Partisans' focus on sheer, raw action. Admittedly, you may stealth your way through the entire game (as I did), but playing it guns blazing on a second run is as much fun as carefully picking stray soldiers and hiding them in bushes. And that is one of the highlights of Partisans 1941: you have so much agency over how each level and encounter plays out, that the replay is value is significant.

There is also a factor which is difficult to measure, but which this game nails perfectly well and that is the [i]epicness[/i] factor. The struggle for the survival of Russia, of the Motherland feels [i]real[/i] . The missions, combat, the objectives, everything is beautifully crafted to immerse us in the harsh and grim reality of the Eastern Front in 1941 and succeeds brilliantly in crafting the narrative that follows the despair that plagued the opening days of Operation Barbarossa, to the jubilant confidence that followed the reversal of the tides of war after German forces were stopped before Moscow. You feel part of that struggle in a most unique way, and throughout dialogues, events and in-game newspaper articles you feel part of the war and immerse yourself in this fight for life and death.

Speaking of whichi, note that the game is called "Partisans 1941" for a reason: the game takes place [i]only[/i] during 1941, so you will not get to participate in the Fall of Berlin or even the Battle of Stalingrad, but it is preceisely this focus on 1941, the first year of the War in the Eastern Front, that makes it such a polished experience: by carefully narrowing down the scope of the game and seeking not to be overly ambitious, the devs deliver a solid and fresh take on such a scantly visited episode of the war: the year 1941 in the Eastern Front, with all that the ebbing and flowing of the tide of war entailed It is a game rich with significance and it is powerful in delivering the message of despair, resistance and ultimately, hope in the face of insurmountable odds.

For all the power of its premise, the game could use some polishing on some elements of its storyline: characters are bland and rather one-dimensional: Soviets are good guys and the Germans -and their supporters- are deviously evil. Admittedly, it would be difficult to think of the Germans in the Eastern Front of anything rather than barbaric, but overlooking the brutality of the Soviets themselves (especially when a Commissar comes into play later in the game) makes this game seem like a veiled tool of propaganda. While useful for the life-or-death struggle narrative, it feels weak and lazy at times to come up with such one-dimensional characters in a game that otherwise is beautifully and painstakingly crafted to depict real-life events as truthfully as possible. Moreover, while most of the missions are rather solid (and there are indeed some truly remarkable ones), there are a few which are rather bland and suffer from poor level design. Thankfully these are the minority among a brilliant selection of maps -and brilliant there are indeed: train station map, I am looking at you!- but they detract from the experience of an otherwise perfectly-crafted game. Sound effects, moreover, do their job perfectly well, but voice acting can come across as rather bland and boring, and the musical score is unrepentantly forgettable.

Having said that, the game is a solid entry on a somewhat overlooked theater of the bloodiest war of all-time, and is a fresh -if biased- outlook on the often forgotten Soviet experience, and it does so in a way that feels as epic as Russian war movies -such as Brest Fortress- feel. And for that I cannot help but commend it.

After finishing this game, I must say, I had a good bit of fun playing it. You know those games that come out year after year that have 1000 hours of content? The ones that have so much stuff that after a while you just get bored of doing it? Sometimes, you just want a game that gives you something fun to play with. Gives you a new toy for a weekend... and right as you start to get tired, it ends. You feel satisfied for finished it, and leave content. This is one of those games.

Story:
You command a group of partisans during the invasion of Russia, starting out small before going on full raids of Nazi compounds. The games story is honestly one of the parts I was a little let down by. There is a lot to be left desired, but at the same time, it's kinda like an early Rambo movie; It's short, sweet, gets to the point, and doesn't throw you around too much along the way. The Nazi's are bad, you kick them in the loins repeatedly as they shout how much better they are, before shanking them in the jugular. That's pretty much it. Characters get introduced, shown off how cool they are, maybe have a quick mission about them, before being just part of the unit.

Gameplay:
The early game is what you would expect of a rag tag group of partisans-- the whole unit has one rifle they found in a garbage can with 4 rounds among them, two rocks, a bottle, and a rusty butter knife. Safe to say, this is when the game heavily encourages stealth. Though you can still go loud, it isn't the best option all the time. Speaking of stealth, this game does a fairly OK job at it. Vision cones that see up to a distance which start to alert guards, or sounds that can be heard through walls or over fences make up most of the sneaking experience. It's simple, it works... kinda. The issue with the game isn't how stealth works, but how stealth goes RIGHT into combat if you screw up. There is no grace period, no short pause to give you a chance to fix your mistake with quick acting, not even a search phase-- 99% of the time, the moment you screw up stealth, everyone knows where your partisans are. They could be in the trees crouched down in the middle of the night, and that still wouldn't require searching. Still though, besides this, stealth is fun... sometimes clunky but fun.

Combat on the other hand is amazingly fun! It's cover based, and % to hit, but besides this, it's a blast to set up an ambush on a huge group and come out on top. Where stealth is slow and methodical, combat is quick and deadly. Someone gets caught in the open, chances are they are going to go down. This applies to enemies too, which can make killing a whole unit all the more enjoyable. Although, I would say the one major issue I had with combat was how later levels it just felt like my squad was a team of unkillable murder machines. The enemies can be... dumb at times; Dumb as in they would not find any immediate cover, and instead, just sit in the middle of the road to be knocked down. Sure they use grenades to flush you out of cover, but never try to flank or do anything more than get to cover and shoot. Due to this, I was driven towards more combat to a point where if the story didn't require stealth, it was guns out for funs out. Alerting the whole map where I was and screaming out 'COME AND GET ME NAZI PIGS!' became custom on missions about halfway through before gunning down droves of the 'well trained' soldiers.

THE INVENTORY IN THIS GAME IS BAD! Ok, maybe not the worst I've seen, but damn did they screw this one up. Sorting items doesn't put similar items together, it just stacks them. So if you want 9mm ammo, you have to dig through the inventory (I'm talking about the one at base), and drag it over. Item slots have to constantly be refilled when used up. It doesn't matter if you have 9 more bandages in the backpack, you have to drag a new set to the hotbar. Resources don't go to whoever has a matching resource when you want to pick them up, so it becomes a game of 'Where's the Weed in the Inventory'. 

Characters are a mixed bag which is something I don't understand. They give you 8 partisans total, which all come with their own abilities and skill trees... but you can only have three at a time with the commander being one 99% of the time. The sad part is many of the characters aren't all that good. Others just do their job better or have more perks that work better. Why have a flashy ability that does next to nothing or requires great positioning to pull off, when I can have Mr. Machinegun man just kill everyone in front of him with his ability? 

Graphics:
This game is amazing for the style they picked. It's colorful, fits the pallet that you'd usually see in a WW2 movie, and goes for a weird realistic/cartoonish feeling. Cartoonish is probably not the right word, but you get what I mean. However, I did have issues with my FPS not being constant even though my rig isn't low end. Some maps that were a bit smaller were perfectly fine, but the moment the map became too big, it was almost always 30 fps during it. 

Final Score:
8.3/10

I read reviews of people complaining about the lack of depth, and general problems with stealth. I did most of my missions in stealth, that's how I prefer to play, and thought it wonderfully enjoyable and tactically challenging. I'd take my time, save occasionally, and normally spend an average of 2-3 hours in a mission. 

I'd try different Partisans, my favorite combo being the female medic, Valya, and Morozov, the knife-wielding thief. He'd whistle and then Valya would quickly and silently chloroform the soldier when he came to investigate, and since Commander Zorin was always along he could chuck the knife if I needed some distance, and Belozarova with her trusty speed and knife-fighting.

I challenged myself to not be found, and not use grenades or guns, but instead, knives, mines, traps, and silence. On occasion you had to use your guns according to the mission parameters, so I always made sure my insurgents had guns and ammo. I've over 60 hours of game play trying various Partisans and different ways to go about tackling the missions.

For the visuals, I think they're fantastic, colorful and yet have that touch of war to it, so it's not too drab and strikes a healthy balance with its color pallet. 

As for the characters and the story, I think it gives a solid but basic outline, if not one-dimensional, and derivative, at times. There's a strong sense of propaganda in the game that fits well with the era. It's a video game first, and many of us know that not all Partisans were like this group, some were the bad guys, too, and that the Soviet Union wasn't all peaches and cream, to put it mildly. 

Moreover, it's refreshing to me, to say the least, to play a game where it isn't Americans winning the war single-handedly, or another D-Day battle, or the Western Allies taking all the spotlight with their propaganda. And on top of that, to actually have it spoken in Russian (instead of being another game exclusively voice-acted in American English) granted me another level of immersion and respect for the game.

Lastly, I always prefer a game where I can play both sides, it's enjoyable to play as the Axis, as well. I wish they had this in the game, but I understand why they don't. And it's, again, unfortunate that certain WWII games (Partisans '41, too) aren't allowed to stop censoring historical symbols because of the laws of the country that the game is made or will be potentially purchased in, or a personal, or group, desire to censor historical symbols they find offensive, while at the same moment being hypocritically supportive of other symbols that might be offensive to others. The censorship of historical symbols is an impotent, and insidious, form of education.

In any case, I'd highly suggest this game, on sale or at its normal price, but to be on the safe side, wait for a sale, there's plenty of reviewers that'll disagree with my personal assessment of the game. An easy thumbs up for a fun and challenging game.

I really wanted to like this game. But some problems in the core gameplay mechanics and UI makes this game far from a great stealth/tactics game. 

CONS: 
- Too much uncertainty. Especially in the enemy AI.

- Enemies outside can see you while you are inside a building: I believe that buildings should be a safe zone. This adds an extra layer to uncertainty.

- There is no use of using guns: Guns have a hit probability depending on distance and cover. I rarely get a single shot kill even if it says above 75% hit chance. Also guns make noise as expected in these style of games like Desperados or Shadow Tactics. But you don't have a clue of who will hear the shot. A simple UI would show that. Uncertainty, uncertainty...

- Patrol path for some enemies are too long: You kill an enemy, then 5 minutes later patrols somehow find that enemy you killed and find you afterwards. 5 mins of gameplay is gone. There is no game speed increase button as in Desperados 3. 

- Enemies are not distinguishable from the background: I have to press ALT key constantly to highlight the enemies. This kills the stealth game feel.

- CONTROLS: This problem is huge. Selecting a character shouldn't be this complicated. If 2 of your characters are close to each other, then it is impossible to select the one you want. 

PROS:
- Base building: Between missions you upgrade your base with the materials you collected during missions.

- RPG Character development: You chose and unlock certain abilities and improve as your characters level up. 

- Quick SAVE / LOAD: This is really quick. 

Final thoughts: This is not a bad game. There is too much of everything. Some AI changes, UI/Control improvements and some simplification would make this game a masterpiece.

Pros:

2. Moderately interesting inventory and weapon systems allow you to customize your loadout. You also have to think about your ammo- you can't just bury your enemy in a mountain of shell casings.

7. Did I mention the part about killing Nazis?

Cons: 
1. The replayability might be a little shaky. I suppose doing it over again while putting together different combat teams for each mission would provide a little variation, but there are some paths through missions that are obviously better than others.
2. In a game that relies on your exhibition of perfect timing, you end up a lot of the time with... less than perfect timing. I reloaded saves a lot, which is good to be able to do (outside of hard mode) but it can be a little repetitive.
3. The dialogue between characters was mildly interesting from a "how do the Russians see WW2?" perspective but it wasn't very likely to make you emotionally invested in them or anything.
4. The AI was sometimes a little dumb. Like enemy soldiers "searching" for my partisans run right through the room my partisans were in without stopping and fighting. By and large, though, it was pretty competent. It made decent use of cover and had a nasty habit of lobbing grenades around when you let a firefight drag on too long...

I'm glad I bought it, but I think this would have gone from "good" to "amazing" if it had been a sandbox. Maybe I can hope they make a sandbox sequel about the French Resistance?

I've been looking forward to giving Partisans a try ever since finishing Shadow Tactics, which I found fantastic. Sadly, Partisans is only a pale shadow of that tactical masterpiece. I thought a similarly styled game set in Soviet WW2 would be fantastic, but unfortunately it just hasn't grabbed me and is overall a letdown. 

While Shadow Tactics is a clean, highly polished, smooth experience, Partisans is workable, but overall clunky and at times challenging to manage. Like many games set in WW2, the colours used are a drab mix of dirty browns, and dusty greens. While not unexpected, it is somewhat disappointing that this hasn't been taken into consideration when designing the game. Brush and undergrowth meant to hide your team is not always apparent, and occasionally you may think you are hidden but one character is not quite inside the bushes.

Speaking of not quite hidden, the stealth in this game could use a lot of work. Most notably, in an early mission I set up an ambush with two characters taking cover behind a fallen tree on one side of the road, and a third character hidden in the tall grass on the opposite side. Using the tactical mode, I ordered my two men taking cover to open fire, and instructed the third to remain hidden. I planned to wait until the enemy patrol was fully engaged then strike at their exposed flank. Not exactly tactical brilliance, but a nice first effort right? Wrong.

As soon as I opened fire, one member of the enemy patrol immediately turned and began firing at my man hiding in the brush. With no cover he very quickly died. No worries, I must have made a mistake and he wasn't properly hidden or I accidentally had him attacking. I quick loaded and tried again. The same thing happened. I tried several more times, convinced there must be something amiss but no, once battle had begun all enemies seemed to immediately know exactly where all my characters were. So much for strategic options.

While Shadow Tactics featured a cast of colourful (literally) characters with clearly defines roles and interesting unique abilities, Partisans has, well, drab brown man with rifle, drab brown man with pistol, and drab grey boy with shotgun. Characters each have an inventory and can equip different items. There are a variety of guns that come in different qualities, and you will need to make sure you have appropriate ammo for each of them. Although each character has their own set of perks they can gain as they level up, many of these are boring, generic, and overlap multiple characters. They are also rather vague. One chain of upgrades is "Improve rifle accuracy > improve rifle accuracy a lot > improve rifle accuracy a huge amount!" Another is "Increase effectiveness of cover." Yawn.

Unlike Shadow Tactics, the unique abilities each character unlock only play a minor part of getting through each level. In fact, these unique abilities are entirely optional. If you don't want to invest any perk points into them, you don't have to, and then your band of green and brown soldiers will be indistinguishable from one another.

In addition to your missions, Partisans introduces a base for you to micromanage. You'll get to send your units out on missions where RNG will determine whether you return victorious with loot or in failure with injuries. You will need to make sure you are also sending your people out to scavenge food, or else you will starve and moral will drop. That's right, you have a moral level to manage as well. You can make a unit spend a day inspiring the others to improve moral, which comes with some general bonuses. If you steal from innocents or fail in missions, your moral will drop.  None of these camp mechanics really add anything to the game, and for the most part are just a frustratingly tedious way of passing time between actual missions.

Now, I suspect the game gets a bit better as you get further into it, but the first couple hours are just so average that I felt no desire to continue playing. I'll compare this game once more to Shadow Tactics in mentioning that each time I sat down to play it I ended up playing for far longer than I'd intended to. I may come back to Partisans at some point to give it another shot, but it's much more likely I'll just wait for the new Shadow Tactics game on its way.

Partisans 1941 is great. You command a cell of partisans in the height of the eastern front war, starting with a three men team and recruit more characters long the way.

Weapons and ammo are scarce and you’ll have to scavenge and distribute ammo between your team members often. 
In between mission you’ll be in your hideout and send you team to collect food, build structures and execute missions by themselves (with certain success chances) in a way that resembles XCOM 2 WOTC. 
The development studio is Russian and that has a strong presence in the game in several ways. It doesn’t follow western culture sensitivities to violence and depiction of war. One of your team members is 13 years old, for example. The projected hatred to the Nazi occupation is high, the atrocities they committed is depicted often. When you take down sentries with a knife there often is a struggle, it’s hardly ever a clean and silent takedown (one of the characters even spit on the corpse as a final gesture). So the overall sense is of a real killing, and a real combat. 
I especially love the fact that the game hands in opportunities to lay down sophisticated ambushes, combined with diversion, explosives use, movement and flanking.
Each of the characters has its own specialties, like explosives, medical, disguise, heavy weapons, knife takedowns and much more. The characters portraits are a bit over the top as you would expect but they are very much like-able.

A quite inventive spin on the real time tactics/stealth formula, "Partisans 1941" holds its own against a pretty tough competition ("Shadow Tactics" and "Desperados III" were both great imo). It's nowhere near as polished or as well thought-out, but it has a lot of heart and tries some new things that we've not seen before in the genre. The ranged combat mechanics are entirely new and allow for interesting tactical approach. It feels like a clever replacement for the view cone system implemented in Commandos 2, and works good enough to actually make ranged combat a viable option. The stealth is okay, but does not provide too many options, so you are likely to alternate between quiet and loud solutions depending on your patience and playstyle. I really appreciate the camp-related mechanics, gathering resources, and sending off people to handle minor tasks - I've been waiting for something like this since the half-assed implementation of this concept in Robin Hood: Legend of Sherwood. I also find it refreshing that the game approaches WWII from the Russian perspective, and even though it's quite clearly a piece of Soviet propaganda, at least it isn't the vomit-inducing American Call of Duty-style propaganda all over again.
